00418d8d-46ad-4f4f-9b56-6231cd1c93f9.subject: mathematics
00418d8d-46ad-4f4f-9b56-6231cd1c93f9.stem: If a = yî + xĵ, b = î + ĵ + k̂ and c = xî + zĵ are vectors such that a × b is perpendicular to c, then
00418d8d-46ad-4f4f-9b56-6231cd1c93f9.explanation: a × b = |î ĵ k̂; y x 0; 1 1 1| = î(x × 1 − 0 × 1) − ĵ(y × 1 − 0 × 1) + k̂(y × 1 − x × 1) = xî − yĵ + (y − x)k̂. a × b is perpendicular to c exactly when (a × b) · c = 0: x × x + (−y) × z + (y − x) × 0 = x² − yz = 0, so x² = yz. Dropping the minus sign of the ĵ-component gives x² + yz = 0; y² = xz and z² = xy come from pairing the components of a × b with the wrong components of c.

007d4d2b-b34d-4665-95a2-330a369e7ee0.subject: mathematics
007d4d2b-b34d-4665-95a2-330a369e7ee0.stem:
The marks of 2,000 candidates in a test are normally distributed with mean 52 and standard deviation 6. Which of the following statements are true?
(A) The mean, the median and the mode of the marks are all equal to 52.
(B) About 1,000 candidates scored more than 52.
(C) The normal curve of the marks is symmetric about 52.
(D) About 68% of the candidates scored between 40 and 64.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
007d4d2b-b34d-4665-95a2-330a369e7ee0.explanation: A normal curve is bell-shaped and symmetric about its mean, so (C) is true, and for this symmetric single-peaked curve the mean, the median and the mode coincide, all at 52, so (A) is true. Because the median is 52, half of the total area lies on each side of it: about 50% of 2,000, that is 1,000 candidates, scored more than 52, so (B) is true. About 68% of a normal distribution lies within one standard deviation of the mean, here 52 ± 6, from 46 to 58. The range 40 to 64 is 52 ± 12, two standard deviations on each side, and holds about 95% of the candidates, so (D) is false.

011bdc0f-c488-4ed1-bd9c-66100095738d.subject: mathematics
011bdc0f-c488-4ed1-bd9c-66100095738d.stem: For the matrix A = [4 3; 2 2], a scalar λ satisfies A² − 6A + λI = O, where I and O are the identity and null matrices of order 2. The value of λ is
011bdc0f-c488-4ed1-bd9c-66100095738d.explanation: A² = [4 3; 2 2][4 3; 2 2] = [16 + 6, 12 + 6; 8 + 4, 6 + 4] = [22 18; 12 10]. Also 6A = [24 18; 12 12]. So A² − 6A = [−2 0; 0 −2] = −2I, and A² − 6A + λI = (λ − 2)I = O gives λ = 2. Reading A² − 6A = −2I as λ = −2 is the sign slip. Squaring each entry instead of multiplying the matrices gives [16 9; 4 4], and its (1, 1) entry 16 − 24 + λ = 0 gives 8; that slip together with the sign slip gives −8.

015bdaee-c7bb-4789-ac68-9778bff9785f.subject: mathematics
015bdaee-c7bb-4789-ac68-9778bff9785f.stem: For the vector a = 2î − ĵ + 3k̂, the sum of squared magnitudes |a × î|² + |a × ĵ|² + |a × k̂|² is
015bdaee-c7bb-4789-ac68-9778bff9785f.explanation: For a unit vector e, |a × e| = |a| sin θ and a · e = |a| cos θ, so |a × e|² = |a|² − (a · e)². Adding over î, ĵ and k̂: the sum is 3|a|² − [(a · î)² + (a · ĵ)² + (a · k̂)²] = 3|a|² − |a|² = 2|a|². Here |a|² = 4 + 1 + 9 = 14, so the value is 28. Directly: a × î = 3ĵ + k̂, a × ĵ = −3î + 2k̂ and a × k̂ = −î − 2ĵ, with squared lengths 10, 13 and 5, which add to 28. Not subtracting the squared dot products gives 3|a|² = 42; taking |a × e|² as (a · e)² gives |a|² = 14; dropping the squares gives 2|a| = 2√14.

0221d710-a478-4fc5-a397-51c66831fd63.subject: physics
0221d710-a478-4fc5-a397-51c66831fd63.stem: In a Wheatstone bridge with arms P, Q, R and S, the arms P and Q are the ratio arms, R is a variable standard resistance and S is an unknown resistance. The galvanometer shows no deflection when R = 400 Ω. When P and Q are interchanged, the null deflection is obtained with R = 441 Ω. The value of S is:
0221d710-a478-4fc5-a397-51c66831fd63.explanation: At balance P/Q = R/S. First balance: P/Q = 400/S, so S = 400 × Q/P. With P and Q interchanged: Q/P = 441/S, so S = 441 × P/Q. Multiplying the two results removes the unknown ratio: S² = 400 × 441, so S = 20 × 21 = 420 Ω (and P/Q = 400/420 = 20/21, two nearly equal arms). The value 1.05 Ω is the ratio Q/P = 21/20, which has no unit of resistance; 41 Ω is the difference and 841 Ω the sum of the two balancing readings.

028fae3a-e7b2-4d6c-af5f-bf30a5aaff2c.subject: computer_science
028fae3a-e7b2-4d6c-af5f-bf30a5aaff2c.stem: Which of the following is an example of structured data?
options: A CSV file with columns name, age, city
Free-form user comments in a single text field
028fae3a-e7b2-4d6c-af5f-bf30a5aaff2c.explanation: Structured data follows a fixed schema like CSV columns, whereas images, audio and free text are unstructured.

02f290b1-4488-424e-8504-acb24df27176.subject: geography
02f290b1-4488-424e-8504-acb24df27176.stem: Which one of the following statements about technopolies is correct?
options: Their landscape is marked by massive assembly structures and large storage areas.
Silicon Forest, near Seattle, is a technopolis in the United States of America.
Blue-collar production workers greatly outnumber the white-collar specialists in them.
Silicon Valley and Silicon Forest are both technopolies in Canada.
02f290b1-4488-424e-8504-acb24df27176.explanation: Technopolies are high-tech industries that are regionally concentrated, self-sustained and highly specialised. NCERT's two examples are Silicon Valley near San Francisco and Silicon Forest near Seattle, and both are in the United States of America: San Francisco is in California, and Seattle is in Washington State, in the Pacific Northwest close to the Canadian border. The nickname Silicon Forest is most often used for the high-tech cluster around Portland, Oregon, the State just south of Washington, and that is in the USA too. So Silicon Forest is a technopolis of the USA, not of Canada. The landscape claim is wrong: the high-tech landscape has neatly spaced, low, modern office-plant-lab buildings rather than massive assembly structures and storage areas. The workforce claim is reversed: highly skilled white-collar specialists greatly outnumber the blue-collar production workers.

02ffc58b-7ac4-41f7-8664-045d11c943fd.subject: economics
02ffc58b-7ac4-41f7-8664-045d11c943fd.stem: If banks are required to keep 10% of deposits as reserves (CRR = 10%) and there is no currency drain, what is the simple money multiplier?
02ffc58b-7ac4-41f7-8664-045d11c943fd.explanation: The simple multiplier is 1/CRR = 1/0.10 = 10 when currency held by public is ignored.

042703b8-ea06-434c-b594-247954b00760.subject: mathematics
042703b8-ea06-434c-b594-247954b00760.stem:
M is a square matrix of order 3 whose entry in row i and column j is i − j. Consider the following statements:
(A) M is a skew-symmetric matrix.
(B) M is a diagonal matrix.
(C) M is a symmetric matrix.
(D) M is invertible.
(E) |M| = 0
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
042703b8-ea06-434c-b594-247954b00760.explanation: Write M from the rule (entry in row i, column j = i − j): row 1 is (0, −1, −2), row 2 is (1, 0, −1) and row 3 is (2, 1, 0). The entry in row j, column i is j − i = −(i − j), so every entry changes sign on transposing: M′ = −M, which is the definition of a skew-symmetric matrix, so (A) is true. A symmetric matrix needs M′ = M; here the entry in row 1, column 2 is −1 while the entry in row 2, column 1 is 1, so (C) is false. Every entry on the leading diagonal is i − i = 0, but a diagonal matrix needs every entry off the leading diagonal to be zero, and the entry in row 1, column 2 is −1, so M is not a diagonal matrix and (B) is false. Expanding |M| along row 1: 0 × (0 × 0 − (−1) × 1) − (−1) × (1 × 0 − (−1) × 2) + (−2) × (1 × 1 − 0 × 2) = 0 + 2 − 2 = 0. So |M| = 0 and (E) is true. A square matrix is invertible only when it is non-singular (|M| ≠ 0), so M is not invertible and (D) is false. The true statements are (A) and (E). Reading the zero diagonal as a diagonal matrix adds (B); taking the middle term of the expansion as −2 gives |M| = −4, which makes M look invertible and gives (A) and (D); swapping the definitions of symmetric (M′ = M) and skew-symmetric (M′ = −M) gives (C) and (E).

064f7b67-0793-4a21-affa-3a9c6d65c3e4.subject: mathematics
064f7b67-0793-4a21-affa-3a9c6d65c3e4.stem: For a Poisson variate X, the probabilities satisfy 5P(X = 3) = 2P(X = 4). The mean of X is:
064f7b67-0793-4a21-affa-3a9c6d65c3e4.explanation: For a Poisson variate with mean m, P(X = r) = e^(−m) m^r / r!. So 5 × e^(−m) m³/3! = 2 × e^(−m) m⁴/4!. Cancel e^(−m) and m³ (m > 0): 5/6 = 2m/24, that is 5/6 = m/12, so m = 10. Check: P(X = 4)/P(X = 3) = m/4 = 10/4 = 5/2, which is what 5P(X = 3) = 2P(X = 4) requires. 2.5 drops the factorials (5m³ = 2m⁴); 7.5 takes the ratio of successive probabilities as m/3 instead of m/4; 1.6 turns the relation upside down (m/4 = 2/5).

086521e1-2f7e-4453-ae3d-d235efa465da.subject: mathematics
086521e1-2f7e-4453-ae3d-d235efa465da.stem:
a, b and c are real numbers. Which of the following statements are true?
(A) If a < b and b < c, then a < c.
(B) If a < b and c > 0, then a/c > b/c.
(C) If a < b and c < 0, then a/c > b/c.
(D) If a > b and c < 0, then a − c > b − c.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
086521e1-2f7e-4453-ae3d-d235efa465da.explanation: (A) is the transitive property of inequalities: if a is less than b and b is less than c, then a is less than c (and in the same way a > b and b > c give a > c), so it is true. Multiplying or dividing both sides of an inequality by a positive number keeps its direction: a < b and c > 0 give a/c < b/c (3 < 6 gives 1 < 2 for c = 3), so (B) is false. Multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative number reverses it: a < b and c < 0 give a/c > b/c (3 < 6 gives −1 > −2 for c = −3), so (C) is true; in the same way a > b and c < 0 give ac < bc. Adding or subtracting the same number, positive or negative, never changes the direction, even when c is negative: a > b gives a − c > b − c (6 > 3 gives 9 > 6 for c = −3), so (D) is true. Only multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative number reverses an inequality, so (B), which reverses it for a positive divisor, is the one false statement.

08bed2f1-75a5-490e-a080-f5217fd83ae8.subject: mathematics
08bed2f1-75a5-490e-a080-f5217fd83ae8.stem: The straight line given by x = 2z + 1, y = 3z − 2 and the straight line given by x = kz + 4, y = 2z + 5 are at right angles to each other. The value of k is
08bed2f1-75a5-490e-a080-f5217fd83ae8.explanation: Write each line in symmetric form. From x = 2z + 1 and y = 3z − 2: (x − 1)/2 = (y + 2)/3 = z/1, so its direction ratios are 2, 3, 1. Similarly (x − 4)/k = (y − 5)/2 = z/1, with direction ratios k, 2, 1. Lines with direction ratios a₁, b₁, c₁ and a₂, b₂, c₂ are perpendicular when a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ + c₁c₂ = 0: 2k + 6 + 1 = 0, so k = −7/2. In general, lines x = pz + q, y = rz + s and x = p′z + q′, y = r′z + s′ have direction ratios p, r, 1 and p′, r′, 1, so they are perpendicular exactly when pp′ + rr′ + 1 = 0. Leaving out the direction ratio 1 of z gives 2k + 6 = 0 and k = −3; a sign slip gives 7/2; using the condition for parallel lines, k/2 = 2/3, gives 4/3.

09eea9aa-9687-498b-8f1c-2a95024de7cb.subject: economics
09eea9aa-9687-498b-8f1c-2a95024de7cb.stem: In a two-sector economy the consumption function is C = 60 + 0.75Y (in Rs crore). If investment rises from Rs 20 crore to Rs 40 crore, the new equilibrium level of income is:
09eea9aa-9687-498b-8f1c-2a95024de7cb.explanation: At equilibrium Y = C + I = (60 + 0.75Y) + I, so Y(1 - 0.75) = 60 + I and Y = (autonomous consumption + I) / (1 - MPC). With the new investment I = 40: Y = (60 + 40) / 0.25 = 100 / 0.25 = Rs 400 crore. Rs 320 crore is the old equilibrium income (80 / 0.25, with I = 20), and Rs 80 crore is only the change in income (20 x multiplier 4), not its level. Rs 100 crore forgets to divide by (1 - MPC).

0a23e819-de4b-4c22-83e4-89ea94574653.subject: physics
0a23e819-de4b-4c22-83e4-89ea94574653.stem: A coil of negligible resistance and inductance 0.35 H is connected to a 154 V, 50 Hz a.c. supply. The rms current in the coil is: (take π = 22/7)
0a23e819-de4b-4c22-83e4-89ea94574653.explanation: The inductive reactance is X_L = ωL = 2πνL = 2 × (22/7) × 50 × 0.35 = 110 Ω. For a pure inductor the rms current is I = V/X_L = 154 V/110 Ω = 1.4 A (the supply voltage of 154 V is its rms value). The value 2.0 A is the peak current, √2 × 1.4 A; 0.99 A treats 154 V as a peak value and divides by √2 again; 8.8 A uses ν in place of ω = 2πν, giving X_L = 17.5 Ω.

0b239ef8-ccb0-4cdd-8f1c-b9def2e9edc9.subject: accountancy
0b239ef8-ccb0-4cdd-8f1c-b9def2e9edc9.stem: A firm is being dissolved, and its stock has a book value of ₹ 60,000. One partner keeps a quarter of the stock, valued at 80% of its book value, and the other three quarters go to outside buyers at 10% above book value. How much cash does the firm receive for its stock?
0b239ef8-ccb0-4cdd-8f1c-b9def2e9edc9.explanation: The stock taken over by the partner is settled through his capital account, so no cash comes in for it: 25% × 60,000 = 15,000 at book value, taken at 80% = 12,000. The remaining stock = 75% × 60,000 = 45,000 at book value. It was sold at a gain of 10%, so cash realised = 45,000 × 110% = 49,500. Adding the 12,000 taken over gives 61,500, applying the gain to the whole stock gives 66,000, and selling the remaining stock at book value gives 45,000.

0c46aa90-0caf-4e35-80eb-52fb4683e211.subject: computer_science
0c46aa90-0caf-4e35-80eb-52fb4683e211.stem: Which type of malicious program copies itself and spreads from one computer to another across a network, without attaching itself to a host file?
0c46aa90-0caf-4e35-80eb-52fb4683e211.explanation: A worm copies itself and spreads across a network without needing a host file, unlike a virus, which attaches itself to a file or program. A Trojan horse disguises itself as useful software, and spyware secretly collects information about the user.

0f03d599-563e-4491-9472-78f48dd5dc24.subject: history
0f03d599-563e-4491-9472-78f48dd5dc24.stem: Which Sultan, impressed by Ibn Battuta's scholarship, appointed him the qazi (judge) of Delhi?
0f03d599-563e-4491-9472-78f48dd5dc24.explanation: Ibn Battuta reached Sind in 1333. Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq was impressed by his learning and appointed him qazi of Delhi, a post he held for several years.

0f39713a-7e46-4375-b27e-f2ae37c125d9.subject: physics
0f39713a-7e46-4375-b27e-f2ae37c125d9.stem:
Consider the following statements about electromagnetic waves.
(A) Ultraviolet rays are preferred to infrared rays for photographing distant hills through haze.
(B) Gamma rays and microwaves travel through vacuum at the same speed.
(C) A charged particle going round a circle at constant speed emits no electromagnetic waves, since its speed does not change.
(D) Once a battery has fully charged a capacitor, the displacement current between its plates is zero.
(E) A charge oscillating with a certain frequency produces electromagnetic waves of that same frequency.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
0f39713a-7e46-4375-b27e-f2ae37c125d9.explanation: (A) is false. Haze is made of very fine particles (dust, smoke, tiny droplets), and such particles scatter short wavelengths much more strongly than long ones (for particles much smaller than the wavelength the scattering falls roughly as 1/λ^4). Infrared, whose wavelength is longer than that of visible light, is scattered much less and gets through haze and mist far better, so infrared, not ultraviolet, is used to see and photograph distant objects through haze and fog. Ultraviolet, of shorter wavelength than visible light, is scattered even more, so it is useless for this. (B) is true: all electromagnetic waves, whatever their frequency, travel through vacuum with the same speed c = 3 × 10^8 m/s; they differ only in wavelength and frequency. (C) is false: accelerated charges radiate electromagnetic waves, and a charge moving in a circle is accelerated all the time even at constant speed, because the direction of its velocity keeps changing (centripetal acceleration). This is why, by classical theory, an electron orbiting a nucleus should radiate and spiral inwards, as NCERT notes before the Bohr model. (D) is true: the displacement current is ε0 dΦE/dt. While the battery charges the capacitor the field between the plates grows and the displacement current equals the charging current; once the capacitor is fully charged the field is steady, so the displacement current is zero (and the conduction current is zero too). (E) is true: an oscillating charge is an accelerated charge; it sets up an oscillating electric field, which produces an oscillating magnetic field, and so on, and the frequency of the wave equals the frequency of oscillation of the charge. The true statements are (B), (D) and (E).

11448e97-cc49-44a6-bdc2-8d2099a05f1d.subject: computer_science
11448e97-cc49-44a6-bdc2-8d2099a05f1d.stem: A relational table has 5 columns and 8 rows. What are the degree and the cardinality of this table, respectively?
11448e97-cc49-44a6-bdc2-8d2099a05f1d.explanation: Degree is the number of attributes (columns), which is 5 here. Cardinality is the number of tuples (rows), which is 8 here. Option B swaps the two terms, and options C and D combine the numbers by addition and multiplication instead of reading them directly.

118c166c-8d63-4a53-9e2e-6fbd994b8dce.subject: chemistry
118c166c-8d63-4a53-9e2e-6fbd994b8dce.stem: For the cell reaction Cu(s) + 2Ag⁺(aq) → Cu²⁺(aq) + 2Ag(s), the standard cell potential E°cell is 0.46 V. Taking F = 96487 C mol⁻¹, the standard Gibbs energy of the reaction, ΔrG°, is:
118c166c-8d63-4a53-9e2e-6fbd994b8dce.explanation: ΔrG° = −nFE°cell, where n is the number of electrons transferred in the balanced cell reaction. Copper is oxidised at the anode, Cu(s) → Cu²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻, and the two silver ions take one electron each at the cathode, 2Ag⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → 2Ag(s). The two electrons copper loses are the same two the silver ions gain, so n = 2 (not 1, and not 4). (E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.80 V − 0.34 V = 0.46 V.) ΔrG° = −2 × 96487 C mol⁻¹ × 0.46 V = −88,768 J mol⁻¹ = −88.77 kJ mol⁻¹, since 1 C × 1 V = 1 J. The negative value means the reaction is spontaneous, as a positive E°cell always gives. +88.77 drops the minus sign; −44.38 uses n = 1; −177.54 counts the electrons twice (n = 4). The same steps give NCERT's Example 2.3: for the Daniell cell, Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s), E°cell = 1.1 V and n = 2, so ΔrG° = −2 × 1.1 V × 96487 C mol⁻¹ = −212.27 kJ mol⁻¹.

124e00d2-25e6-41a3-8351-283f4426bd07.subject: economics
124e00d2-25e6-41a3-8351-283f4426bd07.stem: The price of a notebook rises from Rs 50 to Rs 60, and the number of notebooks bought in a week by the students of a school falls from 200 to 150. Ignoring the sign, the price elasticity of demand for the notebook is:
124e00d2-25e6-41a3-8351-283f4426bd07.explanation: Price elasticity of demand = (% change in quantity demanded) / (% change in price), with both changes measured on the starting value. % change in quantity = (150 - 200) / 200 x 100 = -25%. % change in price = (60 - 50) / 50 x 100 = +20%. So eD = -25 / 20 = -1.25, and its absolute value is 1.25: demand is elastic. Taking the final values as the base gives 2.0, dividing the price change by the quantity change gives 0.8, and dividing the unit changes (50 / 10) gives 5.0.

145c823f-14d1-4d7d-bc81-5107510977c9.subject: mathematics
145c823f-14d1-4d7d-bc81-5107510977c9.stem: If x = t − 1/t and y = t³ − 1/t³, where t > 0, then the derivative dy/dx, written in terms of x and y, is
145c823f-14d1-4d7d-bc81-5107510977c9.explanation: dx/dt = 1 + 1/t² = (1/t)(t + 1/t) and dy/dt = 3t² + 3/t⁴ = (3/t)(t³ + 1/t³), so dy/dx = 3(t³ + 1/t³)/(t + 1/t). Now (t + 1/t)² = (t − 1/t)² + 4 = x² + 4 and (t³ + 1/t³)² = (t³ − 1/t³)² + 4 = y² + 4. For t > 0 both sums are positive, so t + 1/t = √(x² + 4) and t³ + 1/t³ = √(y² + 4). Hence dy/dx = 3√((y² + 4)/(x² + 4)). The version with − 4 belongs to the sum pair x = t + 1/t, y = t³ + 1/t³: there the same steps give dy/dx = 3(t³ − 1/t³)/(t − 1/t), and (t − 1/t)² = x² − 4, (t³ − 1/t³)² = y² − 4, so dy/dx = 3√((y² − 4)/(x² − 4)); using that form for this difference pair is the slip. Squaring the ratio and not taking the root gives 9(y² + 4)/(x² + 4); keeping the 3 but dropping the root gives 3(y² + 4)/(x² + 4).

1fe7b2d3-819c-4607-936f-00626e2ba7c7.subject: computer_science
1fe7b2d3-819c-4607-936f-00626e2ba7c7.stem:
The table EMP is given below.
Empid | Ename | Dept | Salary
101 | Ravi | Sales | 45000
102 | Meena | HR | 52000
103 | Arjun | Sales | NULL
104 | Kavya | IT | 61000
105 | Imran | HR | 48000
How many rows does the query SELECT DISTINCT Dept FROM EMP WHERE Salary > 40000; display?
1fe7b2d3-819c-4607-936f-00626e2ba7c7.explanation: Rows with Salary above 40000 are Ravi (Sales), Meena (HR), Kavya (IT) and Imran (HR), so 4 rows remain before duplicates are removed. The NULL salary row is excluded because NULL > 40000 is not true. DISTINCT keeps one row per department, leaving Sales, HR and IT, which is 3 rows.

204e5691-057d-4b2a-b119-3cc545aec418.subject: business_studies
204e5691-057d-4b2a-b119-3cc545aec418.stem: Riya bought a packaged food item that did not list the expiry date. She later fell ill. Which consumer right is violated, and why?
options: Right to safety, because any illness due to a product often means safety right was violated.
Right to be informed, because the package lacked essential information about safe usage.
Right to choose, because missing date reduces options for similar products.
Right to seek redressal, because she fell ill and needs compensation.

2252c6b1-1287-4af3-9ffa-0e80e71b37a8.subject: mathematics
2252c6b1-1287-4af3-9ffa-0e80e71b37a8.stem:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I:
(A) Mean of a binomial distribution with n = 24 and q = 0.25
(B) Number of trials of a binomial distribution with mean 6 and variance 4.2
(C) Probability of success of a binomial distribution with mean 9 and variance 2.25
(D) Variance of the number of heads when a fair coin is tossed 8 times
List-II:
(I) 0.75
(II) 18
(III) 2
(IV) 20
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
2252c6b1-1287-4af3-9ffa-0e80e71b37a8.explanation: For a binomial distribution with n trials and probability of success p, mean = np and variance = npq, where q = 1 − p. Dividing the variance by the mean gives q. (A) p = 1 − 0.25 = 0.75, so the mean is 24 × 0.75 = 18 (using q in place of p gives 6). (B) q = 4.2/6 = 0.7, so p = 0.3 and n = mean/p = 6/0.3 = 20; check: 20 × 0.3 × 0.7 = 4.2. (C) q = 2.25/9 = 0.25, so p = 0.75 (and n = 9/0.75 = 12). (D) n = 8 and p = q = 1/2, so the variance is 8 × 1/2 × 1/2 = 2; the mean, 4, is a different quantity. Dividing the mean by the variance instead would give q greater than 1, which is impossible: q is always variance ÷ mean.

23fda7f6-04bb-43cf-8611-002db1847e7c.subject: mathematics
23fda7f6-04bb-43cf-8611-002db1847e7c.stem: A machine bought for ₹ 1,80,000 has a residual value of ₹ 30,000 and a useful life of 5 years. Using the straight-line method, its book value at the end of 2 years is:
23fda7f6-04bb-43cf-8611-002db1847e7c.explanation: Annual depreciation = (cost − residual value) ÷ useful life = (1,80,000 − 30,000) ÷ 5 = ₹ 30,000. After 2 years the total depreciation is ₹ 60,000, so the book value is 1,80,000 − 60,000 = ₹ 1,20,000. The figure ₹ 60,000 is only the depreciation charged so far, and ignoring the residual value gives ₹ 36,000 a year and a book value of 1,80,000 − 72,000 = ₹ 1,08,000.

24bb3f55-56dd-4570-8492-c3bce1369bf7.subject: mathematics
24bb3f55-56dd-4570-8492-c3bce1369bf7.stem: The determinant of the adjoint of a square matrix A of order 3 is 49. Then the determinant of the matrix 3A is
24bb3f55-56dd-4570-8492-c3bce1369bf7.explanation: For a square matrix of order n, |adj A| = |A|ⁿ⁻¹. Here n = 3, so |A|² = 49 and |A| = 7 or −7: both signs are possible because the power n − 1 = 2 is even. Multiplying a matrix of order n by k multiplies its determinant by kⁿ, so |3A| = 3³ × |A| = 27 × 7 = 189 or 27 × (−7) = −189. Writing only 189 drops the negative root; 63 or −63 uses 3² (the power n − 1 in place of n); 21 or −21 multiplies the determinant by 3 only, as if |kA| were k|A|.

24da61f4-332d-4048-b169-1a2088c0f0e9.subject: mathematics
24da61f4-332d-4048-b169-1a2088c0f0e9.stem:
Let f(x) = x³ − 3x² − 9x + 5. Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) x-coordinate of the point of local maximum of f
(B) x-coordinate of the point of local minimum of f
(C) Local maximum value of f
(D) Local minimum value of f
List-II
(I) 10
(II) −22
(III) −1
(IV) 3
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
24da61f4-332d-4048-b169-1a2088c0f0e9.explanation: f'(x) = 3(x − 3)(x + 1) gives critical points x = −1 and x = 3. Since f''(x) = 6x − 6 is negative at x = −1 and positive at x = 3, x = −1 is the local maximum and x = 3 the local minimum. f(−1) = 10 and f(3) = −22, so the correct mapping is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

29358098-a746-4bdd-b0fe-a83d09299237.subject: geography
29358098-a746-4bdd-b0fe-a83d09299237.stem: Which iron ore mining area is correctly paired with the State in which it lies?
29358098-a746-4bdd-b0fe-a83d09299237.explanation: Bailadila is an iron ore range in Dantewada district (NCERT spells it Dantewara) of southern Chhattisgarh. NCERT says the Jharkhand belt 'further extends to Durg, Dantewara and Bailadila'; all three are in Chhattisgarh, and NCERT names Dalli and Rajhara, in the Durg area, among India's important iron ore mines. Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh in 2000, so Bailadila is now in Chhattisgarh, not Madhya Pradesh; it is not in Karnataka or Maharashtra either. The other pairs are wrong: Noamundi (with Gua) is in Pashchimi Singhbhum, Jharkhand; Kudremukh is in Chikkamagaluru district, Karnataka; Gurumahisani is in Mayurbhanj district, Odisha.

2b6807ae-c16c-4267-b420-5722c0ed952d.subject: mathematics
2b6807ae-c16c-4267-b420-5722c0ed952d.stem: ∫ eˣ (1/x − 1/x²) dx is equal to (where C is the constant of integration)
2b6807ae-c16c-4267-b420-5722c0ed952d.explanation: Since d/dx (eˣ/x) = eˣ/x − eˣ/x², the integrand is exactly d/dx (eˣ/x). Hence the integral is eˣ/x + C. Option D equals the integrand itself, not its antiderivative.

300047ea-3dc7-4cf4-bc6f-abcb00cd5b7f.subject: mathematics
300047ea-3dc7-4cf4-bc6f-abcb00cd5b7f.stem: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) Scalar matrix (B) Skew-symmetric matrix (C) Row matrix (D) Column matrix. List-II: (I) Aᵀ = −A (II) Order 1 × n (III) Order m × 1 (IV) Diagonal matrix with all diagonal entries equal. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
300047ea-3dc7-4cf4-bc6f-abcb00cd5b7f.explanation: A scalar matrix is a diagonal matrix whose diagonal entries are all equal, a skew-symmetric matrix satisfies Aᵀ = −A, a row matrix has a single row so its order is 1 × n, and a column matrix has a single column so its order is m × 1. Swapping the row and column matrices is the usual slip, because both have only one line of entries.

3179f020-e8f9-48fe-8bc0-10a5a5382128.subject: chemistry
3179f020-e8f9-48fe-8bc0-10a5a5382128.stem:
Arrange the following in increasing order of reactivity towards nucleophilic substitution with aqueous NaOH:
(A) 2,4-Dinitrochlorobenzene  (B) Chlorobenzene  (C) 2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene  (D) 4-Nitrochlorobenzene
3179f020-e8f9-48fe-8bc0-10a5a5382128.explanation: Electron-withdrawing nitro groups at the ortho and para positions stabilise the carbanion intermediate of nucleophilic substitution in haloarenes. Reactivity therefore increases with the number of such groups: chlorobenzene < 4-nitro < 2,4-dinitro < 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene.

317a454e-ddae-4661-900e-a336ac3d0294.subject: mathematics
317a454e-ddae-4661-900e-a336ac3d0294.stem: A courier packet is addressed either to SANJANA or to ANJALI, each being equally likely. Only two consecutive letters of the name, AN, can be read on the label. The probability that the packet is for SANJANA is
317a454e-ddae-4661-900e-a336ac3d0294.explanation: Let E₁: the name is SANJANA, E₂: the name is ANJALI, with P(E₁) = P(E₂) = 1/2, and let A: the pair AN is the one seen. SANJANA has 7 letters, so 6 pairs of consecutive letters: SA, AN, NJ, JA, AN, NA. AN occurs twice, so P(A|E₁) = 2/6 = 1/3. ANJALI has 6 letters, so 5 pairs: AN, NJ, JA, AL, LI. AN occurs once, so P(A|E₂) = 1/5. By Bayes' theorem, P(E₁|A) = (1/2)(1/3) / [(1/2)(1/3) + (1/2)(1/5)] = (1/3)/(8/15) = 5/8. 3/8 is the probability for ANJALI; 2/3 counts only the occurrences of AN (2 out of 3) and ignores how many pairs each name has; 12/19 divides by the number of letters (2/7 and 1/6) instead of the number of consecutive pairs.

33636d72-4374-4537-9069-890858e75d50.subject: computer_science
33636d72-4374-4537-9069-890858e75d50.stem: Start with an empty queue. Perform: enqueue(1), enqueue(2), enqueue(3), dequeue(), enqueue(4), enqueue(5), dequeue(). What is the queue content from front to rear?
33636d72-4374-4537-9069-890858e75d50.explanation: After the two dequeues the remaining elements enqueued in order are 3, then 4, then 5.

34148722-3b98-4ab7-a093-863880075b88.subject: computer_science
34148722-3b98-4ab7-a093-863880075b88.stem:
The table EMP is given below.
Empid | Ename | Dept | Salary
101 | Ravi | Sales | 45000
102 | Meena | HR | 52000
103 | Arjun | Sales | NULL
104 | Kavya | IT | 61000
105 | Imran | HR | 48000
What is the output of the query: SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(Salary) FROM EMP WHERE Dept = 'Sales';
34148722-3b98-4ab7-a093-863880075b88.explanation: The WHERE clause keeps rows 101 (salary 45000) and 103 (salary NULL), so COUNT(*) returns 2. COUNT(Salary) counts only non-NULL values, so the NULL salary is not counted and the result is 1, giving (2, 1).

34e245ae-b9e4-4a51-aed4-23448fb29a87.subject: accountancy
34e245ae-b9e4-4a51-aed4-23448fb29a87.stem: Zed Ltd issued 8,000 9% debentures of ₹ 100 each at a premium of 10%, payable ₹ 30 on application, ₹ 50 on allotment (including the premium) and the balance on first and final call. The issue was fully subscribed. The journal entry for the amount due on allotment is:
options: Debenture Allotment A/c Dr ₹ 4,00,000; To 9% Debentures A/c ₹ 3,20,000; To Securities Premium A/c ₹ 80,000
Debenture Allotment A/c Dr ₹ 4,00,000; To 9% Debentures A/c ₹ 4,00,000
Debenture Allotment A/c Dr ₹ 3,20,000; To 9% Debentures A/c ₹ 3,20,000
Debenture Allotment A/c Dr ₹ 4,00,000; To 9% Debentures A/c ₹ 80,000; To Securities Premium A/c ₹ 3,20,000
34e245ae-b9e4-4a51-aed4-23448fb29a87.explanation: Issue price = 100 + 10 = ₹ 110, paid as ₹ 30 + ₹ 50 + ₹ 30. Amount due on allotment = 8,000 × 50 = 4,00,000. The ₹ 50 includes the premium of ₹ 10, so the part that belongs to the debentures = 8,000 × (50 − 10) = 3,20,000 and the premium = 8,000 × 10 = 80,000. Debenture Allotment A/c is debited with 4,00,000, Debentures A/c is credited with 3,20,000 and Securities Premium A/c with 80,000. Crediting the whole 4,00,000 to debentures ignores the premium, debiting only 3,20,000 leaves the premium out of the amount due, and reversing the two credits puts the premium at the wrong figure.

350e6b60-9039-406a-8e7f-c7d021e04ed4.subject: business_studies
350e6b60-9039-406a-8e7f-c7d021e04ed4.stem: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (standards used to gauge performance): (A) Rate of labour turnover and absenteeism (B) Sales volume and advertising expenditure (C) Quantity, quality and cost of output (D) Capital expenditure, inventories and liquidity. List-II (functional areas): (I) Finance and Accounting (II) Human Resource Management (III) Production (IV) Marketing. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
350e6b60-9039-406a-8e7f-c7d021e04ed4.explanation: Performance standards are set for each functional area. Production uses quantity, quality, cost and individual job performance; marketing uses sales volume, sales expenses, advertising expenditure and the performance of individual sales persons; human resource management uses labour relations, labour turnover and labour absenteeism; and finance and accounting use capital expenditure, inventories, the flow of capital and liquidity. Labour turnover therefore belongs to human resource management, not to production.

35f55f2c-9dff-4ee8-a977-d2268c091670.subject: mathematics
35f55f2c-9dff-4ee8-a977-d2268c091670.stem: The value of ∫₀^(π/2) sin x / (sin x + cos x) dx is
35f55f2c-9dff-4ee8-a977-d2268c091670.explanation: Let I be the integral. Substituting x → π/2 − x gives I = ∫₀^(π/2) cos x / (sin x + cos x) dx. Adding the two forms gives 2I = ∫₀^(π/2) 1 dx = π/2, so I = π/4.

386d01b7-740a-49ed-8930-68da67b0b8bc.subject: mathematics
386d01b7-740a-49ed-8930-68da67b0b8bc.stem: The minimum value of x + 16/x for x > 0 is
386d01b7-740a-49ed-8930-68da67b0b8bc.explanation: Let g(x) = x + 16/x. Then g′(x) = 1 − 16/x² = 0 gives x = 4 for x > 0, and g″(x) = 32/x³ > 0 there, so this is a minimum. Hence g(4) = 4 + 4 = 8.

3aa865f9-ec19-4667-9080-520e967b5b4c.subject: sociology
3aa865f9-ec19-4667-9080-520e967b5b4c.stem: In the classification of tribes, which of the following is treated as an 'acquired' trait rather than a 'permanent' trait?
3aa865f9-ec19-4667-9080-520e967b5b4c.explanation: Tribes are classified on permanent traits (region, language, physical-racial features) and acquired traits (livelihood and extent of assimilation into Hindu society). Mode of livelihood is therefore an acquired trait.

3b2c3c2a-e203-4a75-ac60-525a13070d8c.subject: accountancy
3b2c3c2a-e203-4a75-ac60-525a13070d8c.stem: Kavya and Lata are partners sharing profits in the ratio 3:2. Their capitals are ₹ 2,00,000 and ₹ 3,00,000. The partnership deed provides for interest on capital at 10% per annum. There is no other appropriation, and the profit for the year before charging interest on capital is ₹ 20,000. Interest on capital credited to Kavya is:
3b2c3c2a-e203-4a75-ac60-525a13070d8c.explanation: Interest due: Kavya 2,00,000 × 10% = 20,000 and Lata 3,00,000 × 10% = 30,000, a total of 50,000. The profit of 20,000 is less than this, so interest cannot be paid in full. When profit is not enough, it is divided in the ratio of the interest due (that is, the ratio of capitals), which is 20,000 : 30,000 = 2:3. Kavya gets 2/5 × 20,000 = 8,000. Using the profit sharing ratio 3:2 gives 12,000, paying her the full interest gives 20,000, and an equal division gives 10,000.

3b90d5df-32be-4379-8924-d94eadfd8161.subject: mathematics
3b90d5df-32be-4379-8924-d94eadfd8161.stem:
Two lines are L₁: r = (î − ĵ + 2k̂) + λ(î + 2ĵ − 2k̂) and L₂: r = (3î + k̂) + μ(−2î − 4ĵ + 4k̂), where λ and μ are real numbers. Which of the following statements are correct?
(A) L₁ and L₂ are parallel.
(B) The shortest distance between L₁ and L₂ is √2.
(C) L₁ and L₂ are the same line.
(D) L₁ and L₂ are perpendicular.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
3b90d5df-32be-4379-8924-d94eadfd8161.explanation: The direction vector of L₂ is −2î − 4ĵ + 4k̂ = −2(î + 2ĵ − 2k̂), a multiple of that of L₁, so the lines are parallel: (A) is true. Their scalar product is 1(−2) + 2(−4) + (−2)(4) = −18 ≠ 0, so they are not perpendicular: (D) is false. The point (3, 0, 1) of L₂ lies on L₁ only if (3, 0, 1) − (1, −1, 2) = (2, 1, −1) is a multiple of (1, 2, −2); it is not, so the lines are distinct and (C) is false (proportional direction ratios alone make lines parallel, not the same line). For parallel lines r = a₁ + λb and r = a₂ + μb the distance is |b × (a₂ − a₁)|/|b|. With b = î + 2ĵ − 2k̂ and a₂ − a₁ = 2î + ĵ − k̂, b × (a₂ − a₁) = 0î − 3ĵ − 3k̂, of length 3√2, and |b| = 3, so the distance is √2: (B) is true. Dividing by 6, the length of −2î − 4ĵ + 4k̂, instead of by the length of the vector used in the cross product, gives √2/2 and rejects (B), as does taking |a₂ − a₁| = √6 as the distance. The correct statements are (A) and (B).

3bca44a8-5095-4fdf-ace1-595621a862b2.subject: business_studies
3bca44a8-5095-4fdf-ace1-595621a862b2.stem:
Arrange the following needs in Maslow's need hierarchy, from the lowest level to the highest.
(A) The need to achieve one's full potential through growth and self-fulfilment
(B) The need for self-respect, status and recognition
(C) The need for food, water, sleep and shelter
(D) The need for friendship and acceptance by colleagues
3bca44a8-5095-4fdf-ace1-595621a862b2.explanation: Maslow's hierarchy rises from physiological needs (food, water, sleep, shelter), to safety needs (job security, a stable income, pension plans), social needs (affection, friendship, acceptance), esteem needs (self-respect, autonomy, status, recognition) and finally self-actualisation needs. Self-actualisation is the drive to become what one is capable of becoming, and it includes growth, self-fulfilment and the achievement of goals. It sits at the top, and a person turns to esteem only after the social needs below it are met.

3bf13cad-51cc-46a8-8666-3394de0cb159.subject: physics
3bf13cad-51cc-46a8-8666-3394de0cb159.stem: A pulse of light carrying 9.0 J of energy falls normally on a plane mirror that reflects all of it. Taking c = 3.0 × 10^8 m s^-1, the momentum delivered to the mirror is
3bf13cad-51cc-46a8-8666-3394de0cb159.explanation: Light is a stream of photons, and each photon of energy E = hν carries momentum p = hν/c = E/c. So radiation carrying total energy U carries momentum U/c in its direction of travel: here U/c = 9.0/(3.0 × 10^8) = 3.0 × 10^-8 kg m s^-1. A perfectly absorbing surface takes up all of this, so it receives U/c. A perfect reflector sends the light straight back with momentum U/c in the opposite direction, so the momentum of the light changes by U/c − (−U/c) = 2U/c, and by momentum conservation the mirror receives 2U/c = 2 × 3.0 × 10^-8 = 6.0 × 10^-8 kg m s^-1. The value 3.0 × 10^-8 is the answer for a perfect absorber, not a reflector; 1.0 × 10^-16 and 2.0 × 10^-16 divide the energy by c^2, which gives a mass (E = mc^2), not a momentum.

3c233735-4d2a-49ad-8a53-b2cba9e6d979.subject: computer_science
3c233735-4d2a-49ad-8a53-b2cba9e6d979.stem:
The following Python code uses a list as a stack:

s = []
s.append(10)
s.append(20)
s.append(30)
s.pop()
s.append(40)
print(s[-1], len(s))

What is the output?
3c233735-4d2a-49ad-8a53-b2cba9e6d979.explanation: pop() without an index removes the last element, which is 30, so the list becomes [10, 20]. Then 40 is appended, making the list [10, 20, 40], so s[-1] is 40 and len(s) is 3.

3ca388a2-e0f5-4d73-8690-6e347ed9c763.subject: physics
3ca388a2-e0f5-4d73-8690-6e347ed9c763.stem: Read the statements and select the correct option. Statement I: The magnetic dipole moment of a current loop is given by m = NIA. Statement II: The net magnetic force on a current loop in a uniform magnetic field is zero. Statement III: The torque on a current loop in a uniform magnetic field is independent of the shape of the loop.
3ca388a2-e0f5-4d73-8690-6e347ed9c763.explanation: All three statements are correct. The dipole moment of a planar current loop is m = NIA, the net force on a loop in a uniform magnetic field is zero, and the torque NIAB sin θ depends only on the area of the loop, not on its shape.

3d3a5b97-0249-4275-9f58-5fd7ab90a3d3.subject: physics
3d3a5b97-0249-4275-9f58-5fd7ab90a3d3.stem: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) Lyman series (B) Balmer series (C) Paschen series (D) Brackett series. List-II: (I) Lower level n = 4 (II) Lower level n = 3 (III) Lower level n = 1 (IV) Lower level n = 2. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
3d3a5b97-0249-4275-9f58-5fd7ab90a3d3.explanation: The spectral series of hydrogen are named by the lower energy level the electron falls to. Lyman ends at n = 1, Balmer at n = 2, Paschen at n = 3 and Brackett at n = 4. The Lyman series is in the ultraviolet and the Balmer series is in the visible region.

3dc623cc-4185-4477-b025-b76d7938e6f1.subject: mathematics
3dc623cc-4185-4477-b025-b76d7938e6f1.stem: The area of the region bounded by the curve y = x² and the line y = 4, in square units, is
3dc623cc-4185-4477-b025-b76d7938e6f1.explanation: The curve and the line meet at x = ±2, and the line lies above the parabola on [−2, 2]. The area is ∫ from −2 to 2 of (4 − x²) dx = [4x − x³/3] from −2 to 2 = 32/3. The value 16/3 is the area over only one half, from 0 to 2.

3fc288aa-a85e-4279-8aed-73f9d89b9e7b.subject: mathematics
3fc288aa-a85e-4279-8aed-73f9d89b9e7b.stem: The unit vector a is perpendicular to each of the unit vectors b and c, and the angle between b and c is π/4. Then a is equal to
3fc288aa-a85e-4279-8aed-73f9d89b9e7b.explanation: a is perpendicular to both b and c, so it is parallel to b × c: a = λ(b × c) for some scalar λ. |b × c| = |b||c| sin(π/4) = 1/√2. Since |a| = 1, |λ| × (1/√2) = 1, so λ = ±√2 and a = ±√2 (b × c); both signs give unit vectors perpendicular to b and c. Treating b × c as a unit vector gives ±(b × c); multiplying by sin(π/4) instead of dividing gives ±(1/√2)(b × c); taking |b × c| as sin²(π/4) = 1/2 gives ±2(b × c).

416fed88-c2e1-4723-9f03-f85b5d78dc1e.subject: mathematics
416fed88-c2e1-4723-9f03-f85b5d78dc1e.stem: A function f satisfies 2f(x) + f(1/x) = 3x for every x ≠ 0. Then ∫₁² f(x) dx is equal to
416fed88-c2e1-4723-9f03-f85b5d78dc1e.explanation: Replace x by 1/x in the given relation: 2f(1/x) + f(x) = 3/x. Now there are two linear equations in f(x) and f(1/x). Multiply the first by 2 and subtract the second: 4f(x) − f(x) = 6x − 3/x, so 3f(x) = 6x − 3/x and f(x) = 2x − 1/x. Check: 2(2x − 1/x) + (2/x − x) = 3x. In general, 2f(x) + f(1/x) = g(x) gives f(x) = [2g(x) − g(1/x)]/3 in the same way. Then ∫₁² (2x − 1/x) dx = [x² − logₑ x] from 1 to 2 = (4 − logₑ 2) − (1 − 0) = 3 − logₑ 2. Taking −3/x as +3/x in the subtraction gives f(x) = 2x + 1/x and 3 + logₑ 2; treating f(1/x) as if it were f(x) gives 3f(x) = 3x, f(x) = x and 3/2; putting the 2 on the wrong term, f(x) = [g(x) − 2g(1/x)]/3 = (3x − 6/x)/3 = x − 2/x, gives 3/2 − 2 logₑ 2.

41872980-a987-49d2-8cd1-26271b83aa6d.subject: history
41872980-a987-49d2-8cd1-26271b83aa6d.stem:
Match List-I (early states of the sixth century BCE) with List-II (where they lay).
List-I
(A) Gandhara
(B) Matsya
(C) Avanti
(D) Ashmaka
List-II
(I) In the Deccan, along the river Godavari
(II) In Malwa, around the city of Ujjayini
(III) In the far north-west, around the city of Taxila
(IV) Just west of Mathura, in present-day eastern Rajasthan
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
41872980-a987-49d2-8cd1-26271b83aa6d.explanation: NCERT's Map 1, 'Early states and their capitals', places all four. Gandhara is in the far north-west of the subcontinent, with its cities Taxila and Pushkalavati; only Kamboja is marked further north (A-III). Matsya lies just west of Mathura, the capital of its neighbour Shurasena, and south-west of Kuru and Indraprastha; its land is present-day eastern Rajasthan, around Jaipur and Alwar, and its capital was Viratanagara (B-IV). Avanti, with its capital Ujjayini, lies further south, in Malwa in present-day Madhya Pradesh (C-II). Ashmaka is the southernmost state on the map: it lay in the Deccan, along the river Godavari, far south of Ujjayini (D-I). Read from north to south, the four therefore run Gandhara, Matsya, Avanti, Ashmaka. The commonest slip is to swap the two southern states: Avanti is the one around Ujjayini, and Ashmaka lies well beyond it in the Deccan. Many of the other mahajanapadas, such as Koshala, Kashi, Vatsa, Vajji, Magadha and Anga, lay close together in the Ganga valley.

43e60b95-10cb-4861-822a-678a501c2050.subject: accountancy
43e60b95-10cb-4861-822a-678a501c2050.stem: Tara Ltd purchased equipment from Ravi Ltd for ₹ 2,60,000. It paid ₹ 20,000 in cash and issued equity shares of ₹ 10 each at a premium of 25% for the balance. The number of shares issued to Ravi Ltd is:
43e60b95-10cb-4861-822a-678a501c2050.explanation: The amount payable in shares = purchase price − cash paid = 2,60,000 − 20,000 = 2,40,000. Issue price per share = face value + premium = 10 + 25% of 10 = 10 + 2.50 = ₹ 12.50. Number of shares = amount payable in shares ÷ issue price = 2,40,000 ÷ 12.50 = 19,200. Dividing by the face value of 10 gives 24,000, dividing the whole price by the issue price gives 20,800, and dividing the whole price by the face value gives 26,000.

4413281e-b267-4c9e-b508-d943bdc632b7.subject: mathematics
4413281e-b267-4c9e-b508-d943bdc632b7.stem: The value of a fund grows by 25% in the first year and by 80% in the second year. Its compound annual growth rate (CAGR) over the two years is:
4413281e-b267-4c9e-b508-d943bdc632b7.explanation: Over two years the value is multiplied by 1.25 × 1.80 = 2.25. CAGR is the constant yearly rate that gives this growth: (1 + g)² = 2.25, so 1 + g = 1.5 and g = 50%. Check: 1.5 × 1.5 = 2.25. The average of 25% and 80% is 52.5%, and the total gain of 125% divided by 2 is 62.5%; neither is a compound rate.

445ae24f-2638-45b5-b4e4-eb5f0913d7f1.subject: chemistry
445ae24f-2638-45b5-b4e4-eb5f0913d7f1.stem: Assertion: The boiling point of a solution is always higher than that of the pure solvent. Reason: Boiling point elevation is a colligative property.
options: Both assertion and reason are true, and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.
Both assertion and reason are true, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.
Assertion is true, but the reason is false.
Assertion is false, but the reason is true.
445ae24f-2638-45b5-b4e4-eb5f0913d7f1.explanation: The assertion is true, but the reason is a definition of boiling point elevation, not the explanation of why it occurs (which is due to vapor pressure lowering).

447d2a3e-1a7e-439d-9fd4-069683176986.subject: biology
447d2a3e-1a7e-439d-9fd4-069683176986.stem:
Consider the following statements about the hormonal control of childbirth in humans.
(A) Signals from the fully developed foetus and the placenta set off mild uterine contractions called the foetal ejection reflex.
(B) The foetal ejection reflex triggers the release of oxytocin from the maternal pituitary.
(C) Stronger uterine contractions cut down the further secretion of oxytocin.
(D) Cortisol, estrogens and oxytocin are involved in inducing parturition.
(E) Prolactin is one of the hormones that bring about parturition.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
447d2a3e-1a7e-439d-9fd4-069683176986.explanation: Parturition is induced by a complex neuroendocrine mechanism. Its signals come from the fully developed foetus and the placenta, which set off mild uterine contractions called the foetal ejection reflex, so (A) is true. This reflex triggers the release of oxytocin from the maternal pituitary, so (B) is true. Oxytocin acts on the uterine muscle and causes stronger contractions, and these in turn stimulate further secretion of oxytocin; this stimulatory reflex goes on, with stronger and stronger contractions, until the baby is expelled through the birth canal. The contractions therefore raise oxytocin secretion, they do not cut it down, so (C) is false. NCERT names the hormones of this mechanism as cortisol, estrogens and oxytocin, so (D) is true. Prolactin is not one of them, so (E) is false: its level rises several-fold in the mother's blood during pregnancy, and it is the anterior pituitary hormone that regulates the growth of the mammary glands and the formation of milk (milk production begins towards the end of pregnancy, by lactation), but it does not induce parturition. Of estrogens, cortisol, oxytocin and prolactin, only prolactin is not involved in parturition. The true statements are (A), (B) and (D).

4635494f-c14e-42a9-839b-8745eab4ec6d.subject: accountancy
4635494f-c14e-42a9-839b-8745eab4ec6d.stem: Shine Ltd issued shares of ₹ 10 each at a premium of ₹ 2, payable ₹ 4 on application, ₹ 5 on allotment (including the premium) and ₹ 3 on first and final call. A shareholder holding 500 shares did not pay the allotment money, and the first and final call had not been made. The shares were forfeited and then reissued at ₹ 8 per share as fully paid. The amount transferred to Capital Reserve is:
4635494f-c14e-42a9-839b-8745eab4ec6d.explanation: The shareholder paid only the application money of ₹ 4 per share. The allotment money, which includes the premium of ₹ 2, was never received, so the premium is not part of the forfeited amount. Amount forfeited = 500 × 4 = 2,000. On reissue as fully paid at ₹ 8, the discount allowed = 500 × (10 − 8) = 1,000. This discount is within the forfeited amount of ₹ 4 per share, so it is permitted. Capital Reserve = amount forfeited − discount on reissue = 2,000 − 1,000 = 1,000. Stopping at the forfeited amount gives 2,000, counting the unpaid premium as forfeited gives 500 × 6 = 3,000, and the reserve is not nil because the discount is smaller than the forfeited amount.

48a626c5-4374-472e-b4a9-2590a42dd482.subject: sociology
48a626c5-4374-472e-b4a9-2590a42dd482.stem:
Consider the following statements about soap operas.
I. A soap opera is serialised and continuous: individual stories end, but the soap itself has no ending until it is taken off the air.
II. Buniyaad, aired before Hum Log, was India's first long-running soap opera.
III. Hum Log placed educational content on themes such as gender equality and small family size inside an entertainment programme.
IV. The advertising carried by Hum Log made little difference to Doordarshan, which stayed free of commercial pressure.
Which statements are correct?
48a626c5-4374-472e-b4a9-2590a42dd482.explanation: Statements I and III are correct. Soap operas are stories that are serialised and continuous: individual stories may come to an end and different characters appear and disappear, but the soap itself has no ending until it is taken off the air completely, and it presumes a history that the regular viewer knows, so I is correct. Hum Log (1984-85) was India's first long-running soap opera: some 156 episodes were broadcast in Hindi over 17 months. It used the entertainment-education strategy, intentionally placing educational content in an entertainment programme, and promoted social themes such as gender equality, small family size and national integration, so III is correct. Buniyaad came later, in 1986-87, so II is wrong. Hum Log's advertising promoted a new consumer product, Maggi 2-Minute noodles; advertisers began to line up to buy airtime, and the commercialisation of Doordarshan began, so IV is wrong. Where the genre and its name come from: soap operas began in the United States in the 1930s as daytime radio serials, many of them sponsored by soap manufacturers, which gave the genre its name. They went out in the daytime, when most listeners were housewives, so they were made for a mainly female audience, and women remain the main target audience of most soap operas.

5237c5d2-2fda-4d1c-a92b-e1f119cf4d64.subject: computer_science
5237c5d2-2fda-4d1c-a92b-e1f119cf4d64.stem: Which sorting technique repeatedly finds the smallest element of the unsorted part of a list and places it at the next position of the sorted part?
5237c5d2-2fda-4d1c-a92b-e1f119cf4d64.explanation: Selection sort finds the minimum element of the unsorted part on each pass and swaps it into place, extending the sorted part from the left. Bubble sort swaps adjacent out-of-order pairs, insertion sort places each element into the sorted part, and binary search is a searching method.

5590c1cd-39cf-4740-a079-6156673b0670.subject: mathematics
5590c1cd-39cf-4740-a079-6156673b0670.stem: If A is a square matrix of order 3 such that |A| = 5, then the value of |adj(A)| is:
5590c1cd-39cf-4740-a079-6156673b0670.explanation: Using the property |adj(A)| = |A|^(n-1), where n=3, we get 5^(3-1) = 5^2 = 25.

55e6c5a0-db6b-47d6-8901-71a9a8c983f5.subject: accountancy
55e6c5a0-db6b-47d6-8901-71a9a8c983f5.stem: A company has a net profit after tax of ₹ 1,50,000. It has 10% long-term debt of ₹ 10,00,000, and the rate of tax is 25%. The interest coverage ratio is:
55e6c5a0-db6b-47d6-8901-71a9a8c983f5.explanation: Profit before tax = profit after tax × 100 ÷ (100 − tax rate) = 1,50,000 × 100 ÷ 75 = 2,00,000. Interest on long-term debt = 10% × 10,00,000 = 1,00,000. Profit before interest and tax = 2,00,000 + 1,00,000 = 3,00,000. Interest coverage ratio = profit before interest and tax ÷ interest = 3,00,000 ÷ 1,00,000 = 3 times. Dividing the profit before tax by interest gives 2 times, dividing the profit after tax by interest gives 1.5 times, and adding the interest to the profit after tax gives 2.5 times.

5610ffb8-7ac5-44f3-809b-4ed68c4e9420.subject: mathematics
5610ffb8-7ac5-44f3-809b-4ed68c4e9420.stem: A scholarship fund must pay ₹ 1,200 at the end of every six months for ever. If the fund needed now is ₹ 30,000, the rate of interest per annum, compounded half-yearly, is:
5610ffb8-7ac5-44f3-809b-4ed68c4e9420.explanation: For a perpetuity that pays R at the end of every period, the present value is PV = R/i, where i is the rate of interest per payment period. So i = R/PV = 1,200/30,000 = 0.04, that is 4% per half-year. A year has two half-years, so the rate per annum compounded half-yearly is 2 × 4% = 8%. Check: ₹ 30,000 at 4% per half-year earns exactly ₹ 1,200 every six months and the capital stays intact for ever. 4% is the half-yearly rate left unconverted; 2% halves it instead of doubling it; 16% multiplies it by 4, as if the payments were quarterly.

57b9fb51-2f98-4a1e-a928-b19edc7bbddb.subject: mathematics
57b9fb51-2f98-4a1e-a928-b19edc7bbddb.stem: Two events A and B of a random experiment have P(A) = 3/5, P(B) = 3/8 and P(A ∩ B) = 1/5. The conditional probability P(A′|B) is
57b9fb51-2f98-4a1e-a928-b19edc7bbddb.explanation: P(A′|B) = P(A′ ∩ B)/P(B). The event B splits into A ∩ B and A′ ∩ B, so P(A′ ∩ B) = P(B) − P(A ∩ B) = 3/8 − 1/5 = 15/40 − 8/40 = 7/40. Then P(A′|B) = (7/40)/(3/8) = (7/40) × (8/3) = 7/15. (Check: P(A|B) = (1/5)/(3/8) = 8/15, and 8/15 + 7/15 = 1.) 8/15 is P(A|B), with the complement forgotten; 7/40 is P(A′ ∩ B), not divided by P(B); 7/16 = (7/40)/(2/5) divides by P(A′) and so gives P(B|A′).

59862358-7c7e-4c2b-a3e9-e2fd73c581e7.subject: accountancy
59862358-7c7e-4c2b-a3e9-e2fd73c581e7.stem: A partner retires from a firm, and the amount due to him is to be settled. Which statement about the treatment of his current account is correct?
options: It is carried to the balance sheet of the reconstituted firm as a separate liability, and only the capital account balance is settled with the retiring partner
Its credit balance is added to his capital account (a debit balance is deducted) before the amount due to him is settled
It is first transferred to the Revaluation Account, so that it is cleared together with the profit or loss on revaluation of assets and liabilities
It is paid to him in cash only after the balance sheet of the reconstituted firm has been prepared, without any entry in his capital account
59862358-7c7e-4c2b-a3e9-e2fd73c581e7.explanation: The amount due to a retiring partner is made up of the credit balance of his capital account, the credit balance of his current account, his share of goodwill, reserves and the gain on revaluation, less any debit balance of his current account. So the current account balance is brought into his capital account first, and the capital account is settled afterwards. The full order is: (1) the Revaluation Account is prepared first, and its profit or loss is transferred to the capital accounts of all the partners; (2) the current account balances are closed into the capital accounts; (3) the retiring partner's capital account is settled, by payment or by transfer to his loan account; (4) the balance sheet of the reconstituted firm is prepared last. The current account is not left as a separate liability, and it does not go to the Revaluation Account, which deals only with changes in the values of assets and liabilities.

59a100d2-d92b-48ae-8b1c-773b76b35021.subject: chemistry
59a100d2-d92b-48ae-8b1c-773b76b35021.stem: Benzenediazonium chloride is warmed with cuprous chloride dissolved in hydrochloric acid. The major organic product is:
59a100d2-d92b-48ae-8b1c-773b76b35021.explanation: This is the Sandmeyer reaction. Copper(I) chloride catalyses replacement of the diazonium group by chlorine, with N2 gas released, giving chlorobenzene. Benzonitrile needs CuCN, and benzene is obtained with hypophosphorous acid.

59b0916c-0775-4cf9-9070-878e03330466.subject: mathematics
59b0916c-0775-4cf9-9070-878e03330466.stem: Two taps, A and B, can fill an empty water drum in 10 minutes and 15 minutes respectively, and a drain C can empty the full drum in 12 minutes. Starting with the drum empty, all three are opened together, and the drain is shut 3 minutes before the drum is full. How long does the drum take to fill?
59b0916c-0775-4cf9-9070-878e03330466.explanation: In one minute tap A fills 1/10 and tap B fills 1/15 of the drum, together (3 + 2)/30 = 1/6; drain C empties 1/12. Let the drum be full after T minutes. A and B run for all T minutes, while C runs for T − 3 minutes, so T/6 − (T − 3)/12 = 1. Multiplying by 12: 2T − T + 3 = 12, so T = 9 minutes. Check: A and B fill 9/6 = 3/2 drums, C empties 6/12 = 1/2 drum, net 1 drum. 12 minutes keeps the drain open to the end (net rate 1/6 − 1/12 = 1/12); 6 minutes leaves the drain shut throughout; 7.5 minutes runs the drain for only the last 3 minutes instead of all but the last 3.

5a9aecd3-212f-4efb-a84a-db6bed3a2177.subject: geography
5a9aecd3-212f-4efb-a84a-db6bed3a2177.stem: Which railway gauge accounts for the largest share of the route length of Indian Railways?
5a9aecd3-212f-4efb-a84a-db6bed3a2177.explanation: Broad gauge (1,676 mm) carries most of the Indian Railways route length. Metre and narrow gauge cover much smaller shares, and dual gauge describes a track laid with two gauges rather than a separate gauge.

5aa6c346-d91c-4430-9334-dc8fdf2a627e.subject: geography
5aa6c346-d91c-4430-9334-dc8fdf2a627e.stem:
Consider the following statements about the zones of Indian Railways.
(A) The network is divided into zones because a network this large is hard to manage centrally.
(B) The North Central zone has its headquarters at Gorakhpur.
(C) The East Central zone has its headquarters at Hajipur, in Bihar.
(D) Kolkata is the headquarters of more than one zone.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
5aa6c346-d91c-4430-9334-dc8fdf2a627e.explanation: NCERT explains that the very large size of Indian Railways puts a lot of pressure on a centralised management system, and so the network has been divided into zones; its Table 7.2 lists 17 zones with their headquarters. The North Central zone is headquartered at Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh; Gorakhpur, also in Uttar Pradesh, is the headquarters of the North Eastern zone, so (B) is false. The table gives Hajipur for the East Central zone; Hajipur, in Vaishali district across the Ganga from Patna, is in Bihar, and no other zone has its headquarters in that State. Kolkata, in West Bengal, is the headquarters of the Eastern zone, the South Eastern zone and the Metro Railway, so (D) is true. Hence (A), (C) and (D) are correct.

5bc9735c-eaac-4470-84c1-3d93089740c9.subject: physics
5bc9735c-eaac-4470-84c1-3d93089740c9.stem: A bar magnet of magnetic moment 4.0 A m² is pivoted at its centre and can turn freely in a horizontal plane in a uniform horizontal magnetic field of 0.30 T. It is held at rest with its axis at 60° to the field by a force F applied at right angles to its axis, 12 cm from the pivot. The magnitude of F is:
5bc9735c-eaac-4470-84c1-3d93089740c9.explanation: The field exerts a torque τ = mB sin θ = 4.0 × 0.30 × sin 60° = 1.2 × 0.866 ≈ 1.04 N m, which tries to turn the magnet into line with the field. To hold the magnet at rest the applied force must give an equal and opposite torque about the pivot, F × 0.12 m = 1.04 N m, so F = 1.04/0.12 ≈ 8.7 N (exactly 5√3 N). The value 5.0 N comes from using cos 60° in place of sin 60°; 0.087 N from leaving the distance as 12 (in centimetres) instead of 0.12 m; 0.12 N from multiplying the torque by the distance instead of dividing by it.

5f8c6f5f-5e4a-4381-82e5-edbb509e2463.subject: mathematics
5f8c6f5f-5e4a-4381-82e5-edbb509e2463.stem: Two witnesses, Riya and Kabir, report on the same incident independently. Riya tells the truth 70% of the time and Kabir 85% of the time. The probability that their reports contradict each other is
5f8c6f5f-5e4a-4381-82e5-edbb509e2463.explanation: They contradict each other exactly when one of them speaks the truth and the other does not. They speak independently, so P(Riya true, Kabir false) = 0.7 × 0.15 = 0.105 and P(Riya false, Kabir true) = 0.3 × 0.85 = 0.255. These two cases cannot happen together, so the probability is 0.105 + 0.255 = 0.36 = 9/25. 16/25 = 0.7 × 0.85 + 0.3 × 0.15 is the probability that they agree; 21/200 counts only the first case; 9/20 = 0.3 + 0.15 adds the two chances of not telling the truth instead of multiplying across the two people.

6045c1a6-9b49-426e-ad4e-922024c81a97.subject: mathematics
6045c1a6-9b49-426e-ad4e-922024c81a97.stem: A bank pays interest at a nominal rate of 8% per annum, compounded quarterly. The effective annual rate of interest is:
6045c1a6-9b49-426e-ad4e-922024c81a97.explanation: The effective rate is the rate which, compounded once a year, gives the same interest as the nominal rate r compounded m times a year: effective rate = (1 + r/m)^m − 1. Here r = 0.08 and m = 4, so the rate per quarter is 0.08/4 = 0.02 and the effective rate is (1.02)⁴ − 1. Square twice: (1.02)² = 1.0404 and (1.0404)² = 1.08243216, so the effective rate is 0.08243216, about 8.24% per annum. It exceeds 8% because each quarter’s interest itself earns interest in the later quarters. 8% takes the nominal rate as the effective rate; 8.16% is (1.04)² − 1, compounding half-yearly instead of quarterly; 0.0824% writes the decimal 0.0824 with a per cent sign without multiplying it by 100.

61d6cc6e-f5f9-4b8a-b424-7fcc20a8ad4a.subject: mathematics
61d6cc6e-f5f9-4b8a-b424-7fcc20a8ad4a.stem: Over an 800 m track, cyclist P finishes in 100 seconds and cyclist Q in 125 seconds, both riding at steady speeds. How far behind the finishing line is Q when P finishes?
61d6cc6e-f5f9-4b8a-b424-7fcc20a8ad4a.explanation: Q’s speed is 800/125 = 6.4 m/s. When P finishes, 100 seconds have passed, so Q has covered 6.4 × 100 = 640 m and is 800 − 640 = 160 m from the line: P beats Q by 160 m. Another way: Q still needs the 25 seconds of the time gap, and in 25 s Q rides 6.4 × 25 = 160 m. 640 m is the distance Q has covered, not the margin; 200 m multiplies the 25 s gap by P’s speed (8 m/s) instead of Q’s; 25 m gives the time gap in seconds as if it were a distance.

63dbe2f6-beff-4336-a8e9-435a3e28fe04.subject: chemistry
63dbe2f6-beff-4336-a8e9-435a3e28fe04.stem: In aqueous solution at its isoelectric point, glycine exists mainly as which species?
63dbe2f6-beff-4336-a8e9-435a3e28fe04.explanation: An amino acid exists as a zwitterion, carrying a protonated amino group and a deprotonated carboxylate group. At the isoelectric point the net charge is zero, and the dominant form of glycine is the zwitterion H3N+-CH2-COO-.

6525eda7-fe41-427f-8b9c-d4786ec84c2b.subject: mathematics
6525eda7-fe41-427f-8b9c-d4786ec84c2b.stem:
A and B are invertible matrices of the same order, and k is a non-zero real number. Which of the following statements are true for all such A, B and k?
(A) (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹
(B) (Aᵀ)⁻¹ = (A⁻¹)ᵀ
(C) (kA)⁻¹ = kA⁻¹
(D) (A⁻¹)⁻¹ = A
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
6525eda7-fe41-427f-8b9c-d4786ec84c2b.explanation: (A) is true (NCERT Theorem 4): (AB)(B⁻¹A⁻¹) = A(BB⁻¹)A⁻¹ = AA⁻¹ = I, so the inverse of a product is the product of the inverses in the reverse order; writing it as A⁻¹B⁻¹ is the common slip, and that is wrong in general because matrix products do not commute. (B) is true: using (PQ)ᵀ = QᵀPᵀ, Aᵀ(A⁻¹)ᵀ = (A⁻¹A)ᵀ = Iᵀ = I and (A⁻¹)ᵀAᵀ = (AA⁻¹)ᵀ = I, so the inverse of the transpose is the transpose of the inverse. It is not Aᵀ itself: the matrix with rows (2, 0) and (0, 1) equals its transpose, but its inverse has rows (1/2, 0) and (0, 1). (C) is false: (kA)(kA⁻¹) = k²I, which is I only when k = ±1; the correct rule is (kA)⁻¹ = (1/k)A⁻¹. (D) is true, because AA⁻¹ = A⁻¹A = I says that A is the inverse of A⁻¹, and by NCERT Theorem 3 an inverse is unique.

659edc5d-f549-4be3-aa29-e8c23a2d9b3b.subject: economics
659edc5d-f549-4be3-aa29-e8c23a2d9b3b.stem:
A farmer keeps the area of his land fixed and employs more and more workers on it, one at a time. Arrange the following in the order in which they happen to his total product (TP).
(A) TP reaches its maximum.
(B) TP rises at a diminishing rate.
(C) TP falls.
(D) TP rises at an increasing rate.
659edc5d-f549-4be3-aa29-e8c23a2d9b3b.explanation: This is the law of variable proportions, and it starts from one condition: one input (labour) is increased while the other inputs (land) are kept constant. Total product is the sum of the marginal products, and the marginal product (MP) of the variable input first rises and then falls. While MP is rising, each extra worker adds more than the one before, so TP rises at an increasing rate (D). Once MP starts to fall but is still positive, TP keeps rising, but at a diminishing rate (B). When MP falls to zero, the extra worker adds nothing and TP is at its maximum (A). If still more workers are crowded onto the land, MP becomes negative and TP falls (C). Example: with 1 to 8 workers TP is 6, 15, 27, 35, 40, 43, 43 and 39 quintals, so the MPs are 6, 9, 12, 8, 5, 3, 0 and -4: TP grows faster and faster up to the 3rd worker, more and more slowly from the 4th to the 6th, stays at its maximum of 43 when the 7th worker adds nothing, and falls with the 8th. So the order is (D), (B), (A), (C). (B), (D), (A), (C) puts the diminishing rate first, but MP rises before it falls; (D), (A), (B), (C) puts the maximum too early, since TP keeps rising as long as MP is positive; (D), (B), (C), (A) makes TP fall before it reaches its maximum, but TP can fall only after it has passed its maximum.

664b7a77-53bc-4c82-889a-5731832693ac.subject: physics
664b7a77-53bc-4c82-889a-5731832693ac.stem: For a photosensitive metal, the stopping potential is V0 for light of wavelength λ and 3V0 for light of wavelength λ/2. The threshold wavelength of the metal is:
664b7a77-53bc-4c82-889a-5731832693ac.explanation: Einstein’s equation gives eV0 = hc/λ − φ and 3eV0 = 2hc/λ − φ. Subtracting, hc/λ = 2eV0, so φ = hc/λ − eV0 = eV0 = hc/(2λ), and the threshold wavelength is hc/φ = 2λ. Reading the 3 : 1 ratio of stopping potentials as a ratio of wavelengths gives 3λ, which ignores the work function.

66f791a5-a4e6-4377-afbe-4eef78e000c5.subject: geography
66f791a5-a4e6-4377-afbe-4eef78e000c5.stem:
Consider the following statements about the tertiary and quaternary sectors:
(A) Tertiary activities include services such as transport, trade and banking.
(B) Quaternary activities are knowledge-based and cover research, information technology and data processing.
(C) Tertiary activities directly extract raw materials such as minerals and timber from the earth.
(D) Quaternary activities belong to the primary sector because they use natural resources.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
66f791a5-a4e6-4377-afbe-4eef78e000c5.explanation: Statements (A) and (B) are correct, since tertiary activities are services and quaternary activities are knowledge-based. Statement (C) describes primary extraction, not tertiary activity, and statement (D) is false because quaternary activities are services, not primary activities.

67910760-3c36-4917-9ca7-79fa4315f9c4.subject: mathematics
67910760-3c36-4917-9ca7-79fa4315f9c4.stem: If y = [(1 + x)/(1 − x)]^(3/2), where −1 < x < 1, then (1 − x²) dy/dx − 3y is equal to
67910760-3c36-4917-9ca7-79fa4315f9c4.explanation: Take logarithms (allowed, since (1 + x)/(1 − x) > 0 for −1 < x < 1): log y = (3/2)[log(1 + x) − log(1 − x)]. Differentiate with respect to x: (1/y) dy/dx = (3/2)[1/(1 + x) + 1/(1 − x)], because the derivative of log(1 − x) is −1/(1 − x). The bracket is [(1 − x) + (1 + x)]/(1 − x²) = 2/(1 − x²), so (1/y) dy/dx = 3/(1 − x²) and (1 − x²) dy/dx = 3y. Hence (1 − x²) dy/dx − 3y = 0. Missing the minus sign from log(1 − x) gives the bracket −2x/(1 − x²) and the value −3y(1 + x); using the factor 1/2 of a square root in place of 3/2 gives y − 3y = −2y; dropping the factor 3/2 altogether gives 2y − 3y = −y.

68269c81-6197-4788-9aa3-216209c5f515.subject: biology
68269c81-6197-4788-9aa3-216209c5f515.stem:
In NCERT's diagram of trophic levels in an ecosystem, each organism below is shown at a different level. Arrange them from the first (lowest) trophic level to the highest.
(A) Wolf
(B) Lion
(C) Grass
(D) Grasshopper
68269c81-6197-4788-9aa3-216209c5f515.explanation: NCERT's Figure 12.2 places producers (plants) at the first trophic level: phytoplankton, grass, trees. Herbivores, the primary consumers, are at the second: zooplankton, grasshopper and cow. Carnivores, the secondary consumers, are at the third: birds, fishes, wolf. Top carnivores, the tertiary consumers, are at the fourth: man, lion. So grass (first), grasshopper (second), wolf (third) and lion (fourth) give (C), (D), (A), (B). Putting the wolf before the grasshopper makes a carnivore the plant eater; starting with the grasshopper forgets that every grazing chain begins with a producer; and placing the lion below the wolf swaps the top carnivore with the secondary consumer. The diagram shows levels, not fixed species: a real animal can feed at more than one level, as a sparrow does when it eats seeds and also insects.

691312f0-4190-4917-b995-51cf5cc405ae.subject: mathematics
691312f0-4190-4917-b995-51cf5cc405ae.stem: Which of the following is a sample statistic rather than a population parameter?
691312f0-4190-4917-b995-51cf5cc405ae.explanation: A sample mean is computed from observed data and is a statistic, while μ, σ², p denote population parameters.

6a0c3146-b6d0-45b3-a9eb-f5dfaed0c1ec.subject: geography
6a0c3146-b6d0-45b3-a9eb-f5dfaed0c1ec.stem:
Arrange the following major ports on the western coast of India in order from north to south:
(A) Mangaluru
(B) Kandla
(C) Kochi
(D) Mumbai
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
6a0c3146-b6d0-45b3-a9eb-f5dfaed0c1ec.explanation: Kandla in Gujarat lies at about 23 degrees north, Mumbai at about 19 degrees north, Mangaluru at about 13 degrees north and Kochi at about 10 degrees north. The north-to-south order is therefore (B), (D), (A), (C).

6a10c022-27e2-4ee4-b08b-03f4fcdac734.subject: physics
6a10c022-27e2-4ee4-b08b-03f4fcdac734.stem: A solenoid 40 cm long is wound with 800 turns. The magnetic field well inside it, near its centre, is 6.28 × 10^-3 T. The current in the solenoid is: (μ0 = 4π × 10^-7 T m A^-1)
6a10c022-27e2-4ee4-b08b-03f4fcdac734.explanation: Inside a long solenoid B = μ0 n I, where n is the number of turns per unit length: n = 800/0.40 m = 2000 per metre. So I = B/(μ0 n) = (6.28 × 10^-3)/(4π × 10^-7 × 2000) = (6.28 × 10^-3)/(2.512 × 10^-3) = 2.5 A. The value 5.0 A comes from using μ0 n I/2, the field at an end of the solenoid, instead of μ0 n I; 6.25 A from putting the total number of turns N in place of n; 15.6 A from multiplying N by the length instead of dividing by it.

6a46890c-13bd-4b83-8b37-939ca17ffa22.subject: computer_science
6a46890c-13bd-4b83-8b37-939ca17ffa22.stem: How many passes does bubble sort make to sort a list of 8 elements?
6a46890c-13bd-4b83-8b37-939ca17ffa22.explanation: Each iteration through the elements of the list is called a pass. In every pass bubble sort compares adjacent elements and swaps them when they are out of order, so the largest remaining element 'bubbles up' to its correct place at the end, and that element is left out of the later passes. NCERT states that for a list with n elements, bubble sort makes a total of n - 1 passes: once n - 1 elements are in their places, the last one is already in place. Here n = 8, so 8 - 1 = 7 passes. In the same way a list of 6 elements needs 5 passes, as in NCERT's Figure 5.1, where the list was already sorted in the 4th pass but the technique still made the 5th pass. 28 is the number of comparisons (7 + 6 + 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1), not of passes; 64 is n squared, the order of bubble sort's time complexity; 8 counts one pass per element.

6b359ce9-6dc9-49a5-8ad2-fdecd273f239.subject: chemistry
6b359ce9-6dc9-49a5-8ad2-fdecd273f239.stem: For a reaction, the experimentally determined rate law is rate = k[A][B]^(3/2). The overall order of the reaction is:
6b359ce9-6dc9-49a5-8ad2-fdecd273f239.explanation: The overall order is the sum of the powers of the concentration terms in the rate law, here 1 + 3/2 = 5/2. Order is obtained only from experiment and can be a fraction or zero, unlike molecularity.

6c960f04-5242-4f58-a6f0-60015f6bc800.subject: history
6c960f04-5242-4f58-a6f0-60015f6bc800.stem:
Match List-I (structures at Vijayanagara) with List-II (features).
List-I
(A) Hiriya canal
(B) Vitthala temple
(C) Lotus Mahal
(D) Kamalapuram tank
List-II
(I) Built in the early fifteenth century to store rainwater; its water was also carried by a channel to the royal centre
(II) A chariot street ran in a straight line from its gopuram
(III) Drew water from a dam across the Tungabhadra to irrigate the valley between the sacred centre and the urban core
(IV) Given its name by British travellers in the nineteenth century
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
6c960f04-5242-4f58-a6f0-60015f6bc800.explanation: Vijayanagara lay in one of the most arid zones of the peninsula, so elaborate arrangements were made to store rainwater. The most important tank, built in the early years of the fifteenth century, is now called the Kamalapuram tank: it irrigated nearby fields and its water was carried by a channel to the royal centre (D-I). The Hiriya canal, built apparently by the Sangama kings, drew water from a dam across the Tungabhadra and irrigated the valley between the sacred centre and the urban core (A-III). The Vitthala temple, dedicated to Vitthala, a form of Vishnu worshipped in Maharashtra, has several halls and a shrine designed as a chariot; like the other great temple complexes it had a chariot street running in a straight line from its gopuram, paved with stone slabs and lined with pillared pavilions where merchants set up shops. The Vitthala temple's own chariot street runs east from its main gopuram (B-II). The Lotus Mahal in the royal centre was so named by British travellers in the nineteenth century (C-IV). Two other royal-centre structures: the Mahanavami dibba was a massive platform, and the Hazara Rama temple was probably meant to be used only by the king and his family.

6dcb8cfe-0adc-4195-98f4-5226d9f244e2.subject: chemistry
6dcb8cfe-0adc-4195-98f4-5226d9f244e2.stem:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Compound)
(A) Methylene chloride, CH₂Cl₂
(B) Chloroform, CHCl₃
(C) Iodoform, CHI₃
(D) DDT
List-II (Use)
(I) Insecticide
(II) Once used as an antiseptic
(III) Solvent used as a paint remover
(IV) Production of the freon refrigerant R-22
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
6dcb8cfe-0adc-4195-98f4-5226d9f244e2.explanation: Methylene chloride is the common name of dichloromethane, CH₂Cl₂: NCERT heads its section "Dichloromethane (Methylene chloride)" and lists CH₂Cl₂ as methylene chloride (common name) and dichloromethane (IUPAC name). It is widely used as a solvent, as a paint remover, as a propellant in aerosols and as a process solvent in the manufacture of drugs, so (A)-(III). Chloroform (trichloromethane, CHCl₃) is a solvent for fats, alkaloids and iodine; its major use today is in the production of the freon refrigerant R-22, and it was once a general anaesthetic, since replaced by safer ones such as ether, so (B)-(IV). Iodoform (triiodomethane, CHI₃) was used earlier as an antiseptic, but the antiseptic action comes from the free iodine it liberates, not from iodoform itself; because of its objectionable smell it has been replaced by other iodine formulations, so (C)-(II). DDT (p,p′-dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane) was the first chlorinated organic insecticide, so (D)-(I). The paint remover is therefore methylene chloride. Option A swaps the uses of methylene chloride and chloroform; options B and D give the paint remover or the refrigerant to iodoform.

6ea07aa6-eb31-4f94-a5c1-f9761ea75103.subject: computer_science
6ea07aa6-eb31-4f94-a5c1-f9761ea75103.stem: Relation STUDENT has 5 attributes and 6 tuples, and relation CLUB has 3 attributes and 4 tuples. What are the degree and the cardinality of the relation STUDENT X CLUB obtained by their Cartesian product?
6ea07aa6-eb31-4f94-a5c1-f9761ea75103.explanation: The Cartesian product pairs every tuple of the first relation with every tuple of the second, and each resulting tuple carries all the attributes of both. So the degree of the result is the sum of the degrees of the two relations, and its cardinality is the product of their cardinalities. Degree = 5 + 3 = 8. Cardinality = 6 x 4 = 24. NCERT's own example works the same way: DANCE and MUSIC are both of degree 3, with cardinalities 4 and 5, so DANCE X MUSIC has degree 3 + 3 = 6 and cardinality 4 x 5 = 20. Option A multiplies the degrees and adds the cardinalities (the two rules swapped); option B adds both; option C multiplies both.

70291c3b-d5ad-4b37-989e-2f7f88c6cba6.subject: accountancy
70291c3b-d5ad-4b37-989e-2f7f88c6cba6.stem: Meera and Naveen are partners. On 1 April 2025 their capitals were ₹ 3,00,000 and ₹ 2,00,000. On 1 August 2025 Meera brought in ₹ 60,000 as additional capital, and on 1 January 2026 she withdrew ₹ 24,000 from her capital. The partnership deed allows interest on capital at 6% per annum. Interest on capital payable to Meera for the year ended 31 March 2026 is:
70291c3b-d5ad-4b37-989e-2f7f88c6cba6.explanation: Interest on capital is worked for the period each amount stayed in the firm, up to 31 March. Interest on the opening capital for 12 months = 3,00,000 × 6% = 18,000. Interest on the addition for 8 months (1 August to 31 March) = 60,000 × 6% × 8/12 = 2,400, which is added. Interest on the withdrawal for 3 months (1 January to 31 March) = 24,000 × 6% × 3/12 = 360, which is deducted because that capital was not in the firm for those months. Interest = 18,000 + 2,400 − 360 = 20,040. Charging interest for a full year on the net capital of 3,36,000 gives 20,160, ignoring the withdrawal gives 20,400, and adding the withdrawal instead of deducting it gives 20,760.

73fd584b-e7ae-410e-9954-92afabb63682.subject: mathematics
73fd584b-e7ae-410e-9954-92afabb63682.stem: A loan of ₹ 60,000 is taken at 10% per annum flat rate for 2 years and is repaid in equal monthly instalments. The EMI under the flat rate method is:
73fd584b-e7ae-410e-9954-92afabb63682.explanation: Under the flat rate method interest is charged on the original principal for the whole period: 60,000 × 10% × 2 = ₹ 12,000. Total repayment = 60,000 + 12,000 = ₹ 72,000, and spreading it over 2 × 12 = 24 months gives 72,000 ÷ 24 = ₹ 3,000. The figure ₹ 2,500 is the principal alone divided by 24, leaving out the interest.

75bc29fb-5f94-405b-b6a4-9d121f46ff9e.subject: physics
75bc29fb-5f94-405b-b6a4-9d121f46ff9e.stem:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) Silicon doped with arsenic (B) Silicon doped with indium (C) p-n junction under forward bias (D) p-n junction under reverse bias
List-II: (I) Holes are the majority carriers (II) Narrow depletion layer and large current (III) Electrons are the majority carriers (IV) Wide depletion layer and very small current
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
75bc29fb-5f94-405b-b6a4-9d121f46ff9e.explanation: Arsenic has five valence electrons and makes silicon n-type, with electrons as the majority carriers; indium has three and makes it p-type, with holes as the majority carriers.
