dee791a1-239d-40dd-9522-b59c70abbc99.stem: The price p (in ₹) at which x units of a product can be sold is given by p = 300 − 4x − x². The marginal revenue when 6 units are sold is:
dee791a1-239d-40dd-9522-b59c70abbc99.explanation: Total revenue R = price × quantity = x(300 − 4x − x²) = 300x − 4x² − x³. Marginal revenue is the rate of change of total revenue with respect to the number of units sold: MR = dR/dx = 300 − 8x − 3x². At x = 6, MR = 300 − 48 − 108 = ₹ 144. ₹ 240 is the price p(6), the average revenue, not the marginal revenue; ₹ 1,440 is the total revenue R(6) = 6 × 240; ₹ 224 adds dp/dx = −4 − 2x = −16 to the price without multiplying it by x, whereas MR = p + x(dp/dx) = 240 + 6 × (−16) = 144.

defeb784-7aff-4d43-9292-362d8af7362a.subject: mathematics
defeb784-7aff-4d43-9292-362d8af7362a.stem: The corner points of the feasible region determined by the system of linear constraints are (0, 3), (1, 1), and (3, 0). If Z = px + qy (p, q > 0), the condition on p and q so that the minimum of Z occurs at both (3, 0) and (1, 1) is:
defeb784-7aff-4d43-9292-362d8af7362a.explanation: If the minimum occurs at two points, Z(3,0) = Z(1,1). So, 3p + 0q = p + q => 2p = q => p = q/2.

e0336aca-26f0-46d6-bbc5-2177bccf48d3.subject: physics
e0336aca-26f0-46d6-bbc5-2177bccf48d3.stem: A circular coil of mean diameter 14 cm is held with its plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field. The field is reduced steadily from 0.50 T to 0.10 T in 0.20 s, and an emf of 3.08 V is induced in the coil. The number of turns in the coil is: (take π = 22/7)
e0336aca-26f0-46d6-bbc5-2177bccf48d3.explanation: The area of each turn is A = π(D/2)² = (22/7) × (0.07 m)² = 0.0154 m². The flux through each turn changes by A × ΔB = 0.0154 × (0.50 − 0.10) = 6.16 × 10^-3 Wb in 0.20 s, so the emf induced in one turn is 6.16 × 10^-3/0.20 = 0.0308 V. By Faraday's law the emf of N turns is ε = N dΦ/dt, so N = 3.08/0.0308 = 100. The value 25 comes from using the diameter as the radius (four times the area); 400 from using the final field 0.10 T instead of the change of 0.40 T; 80 from using the initial field 0.50 T instead of the change.

e1b72304-b6c3-4a73-adaf-414b30351497.subject: mathematics
e1b72304-b6c3-4a73-adaf-414b30351497.stem:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) For vectors a and b with |a| = √10, |b| = 5 and |a × b| = 15, the value of |a · b|
(B) The value of p for which the vectors 4î − 2ĵ + 6k̂ and pî − 3ĵ + 9k̂ are collinear
(C) The value of λ for which the vectors î + 2ĵ − k̂ and 3î + λĵ + 5k̂ are perpendicular
(D) The value of (ĵ × k̂) · î + (k̂ × î) · ĵ + (î × ĵ) · k̂
List-II
(I) 5
(II) 1
(III) 6
(IV) 3
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
e1b72304-b6c3-4a73-adaf-414b30351497.explanation: (A) |a × b| = |a||b| sin θ and |a · b| = |a||b| |cos θ|, so |a × b|² + (a · b)² = |a|²|b|². Hence (a · b)² = 10 × 25 − 15² = 250 − 225 = 25 and |a · b| = 5. (B) Collinear vectors have proportional components: p/4 = (−3)/(−2) = 9/6 = 3/2, so p = 6. (C) Perpendicular vectors have zero scalar product: 1(3) + 2(λ) + (−1)(5) = 2λ − 2 = 0, so λ = 1. (D) ĵ × k̂ = î, k̂ × î = ĵ and î × ĵ = k̂, so each term is 1 and the sum is 3. So (A) - (I), (B) - (III), (C) - (II), (D) - (IV). Writing k̂ × î = −ĵ makes the sum in (D) equal to 1, the pairing that swaps (C) and (D); the other two pairings put 3 or 6 against |a · b|, which needs (a · b)² = 25.

e1d200a2-f90b-488f-a4a1-61f1e268496e.subject: physics
e1d200a2-f90b-488f-a4a1-61f1e268496e.stem: A wire carrying a current of 6.0 A comes in along a straight line directed towards a point O, follows a circular arc of radius 2.0 cm centred on O through one quarter of a circle (90°), and leaves along a straight line directed away from O. The magnitude of the magnetic field at O is: (μ0 = 4π × 10^-7 T m A^-1)
e1d200a2-f90b-488f-a4a1-61f1e268496e.explanation: For every element of the two straight parts, dl lies along the line joining it to O, so dl × r = 0 and the straight parts add nothing to the field at O. Every element of the arc is at the same distance R from O and gives a field in the same direction, so an arc subtending an angle θ at O gives the fraction θ/2π of the field at the centre of a full circular loop. Full loop: μ0 I/(2R) = (4π × 10^-7 × 6.0)/(2 × 0.020) = 1.9 × 10^-4 T. A quarter of it is 4.7 × 10^-5 T. The value 1.9 × 10^-4 T is the field of a full loop; 1.4 × 10^-4 T takes the remaining three-quarters of the circle instead of the arc; 6.0 × 10^-5 T uses the formula μ0 I/(2πR) for a long straight wire.

e507a240-c420-4b53-a27d-be8c70f5ccb5.subject: geography
e507a240-c420-4b53-a27d-be8c70f5ccb5.stem: India and China are the only two countries with more than a billion people each. Which country comes next in the world's population ranking?
e507a240-c420-4b53-a27d-be8c70f5ccb5.explanation: By UN estimates for 2024, the United States of America is the third most populous country in the world, with about 345 million people, far behind India and China (about 1.4 billion each; India passed China in 2023). Indonesia (about 283 million) is fourth and Pakistan (about 251 million) fifth; Nigeria, Brazil and Bangladesh come next, and Russia (about 145 million) is ninth. NCERT's Fig. 2.1, drawn from older figures, shows China first and Brazil ahead of Pakistan, but it too puts the USA third. NCERT notes that the 10 most populous countries hold about 60 per cent of the world's people and that 6 of them are in Asia; the USA is the most populous country outside Asia.

e8ef1d10-e1ce-4efd-9ff5-9d2d815c0595.subject: economics
e8ef1d10-e1ce-4efd-9ff5-9d2d815c0595.stem: An economy produces only rice. In 2018 it produced 500 quintals at Rs 40 per quintal, and in 2019 it produced 600 quintals at Rs 55 per quintal. Taking 2018 as the base year, the real GDP of 2019 is:
e8ef1d10-e1ce-4efd-9ff5-9d2d815c0595.explanation: Real GDP is the output of the current year valued at the prices of the base year: real GDP of 2019 = quantity of 2019 x price of 2018 = 600 x 40 = Rs 24,000. Rs 33,000 (600 x 55) is the nominal GDP of 2019, because it uses current prices. Rs 20,000 (500 x 40) is the GDP of the base year itself, and Rs 27,500 (500 x 55) mixes the old quantity with the new price.

e9b39e3c-100c-4d72-be16-548adc1748df.subject: business_studies
e9b39e3c-100c-4d72-be16-548adc1748df.stem:
Consider the following activities.
(A) Providing scope, within the provisions of law, for a controlled degree of speculation
(B) Ensuring the safety of transactions through well-regulated membership and clearly defined dealings
(C) Deciding, through its governing board, the price at which each listed share must be bought and sold
(D) Channelling savings into their most productive uses through disinvestment and reinvestment
(E) Creating a continuous market in which investors can convert their existing securities into cash
Which of these are functions of a stock exchange?
e9b39e3c-100c-4d72-be16-548adc1748df.explanation: NCERT lists six functions of a stock exchange. (1) It provides liquidity and marketability to existing securities: it creates a continuous market in which investors can convert their securities into cash, which is (E). (2) It helps in the pricing of securities: prices are set by the forces of demand and supply on the exchange, not decided by its governing board, so (C) is not a function. (3) It ensures the safety of transactions: its membership is well regulated and its dealings follow a defined legal framework, so the investing public gets a safe and fair deal, which is (B). (4) It contributes to economic growth: through disinvestment and reinvestment, savings are channelled into their most productive investment avenues, leading to capital formation, which is (D). (5) It spreads the equity cult. (6) It provides scope for speculation within the provisions of law, in a restricted and controlled manner, because a certain degree of healthy speculation is needed for liquidity and price continuity in the market, which is (A). So a stock exchange does not try to put a complete stop to speculation; it allows healthy speculation under control. The functions are (A), (B), (D) and (E).

e9cac0e5-90eb-4240-bdd4-a3f901a2e7e0.subject: psychology
e9cac0e5-90eb-4240-bdd4-a3f901a2e7e0.stem: Systematic desensitisation, a technique used in the treatment of phobias, was developed by:
e9cac0e5-90eb-4240-bdd4-a3f901a2e7e0.explanation: Systematic desensitisation was developed by Joseph Wolpe and is based on classical conditioning and counterconditioning of anxiety with relaxation. Rogers founded client-centred therapy, Skinner operant conditioning and Beck cognitive therapy.

eab7b9e0-c086-4422-8820-f49e7701fe40.subject: physics
eab7b9e0-c086-4422-8820-f49e7701fe40.stem: An alpha particle of kinetic energy 7.2 MeV approaches a tin nucleus (atomic number 50) head-on. Taking e²/(4πε₀) = 1.44 MeV fm, the distance of closest approach is:
eab7b9e0-c086-4422-8820-f49e7701fe40.explanation: At the closest approach all the kinetic energy has become electrostatic potential energy: K = (2e)(Ze)/(4πε₀r₀), so r₀ = 2Z × 1.44 MeV fm / K = (2 × 50 × 1.44)/7.2 = 20 fm. Leaving out the charge 2e of the alpha particle gives 10 fm.

ed2b7448-3d0f-4e70-9e56-ba29ba3bc47a.subject: mathematics
ed2b7448-3d0f-4e70-9e56-ba29ba3bc47a.stem: The maximum value of f(x) = x³ − 3x on the interval [−2, 2] is
ed2b7448-3d0f-4e70-9e56-ba29ba3bc47a.explanation: f'(x) = 3x² − 3 = 0 gives x = ±1. The values are f(−2) = −2, f(−1) = 2, f(1) = −2 and f(2) = 2, so the greatest value on [−2, 2] is 2, attained at x = −1 and x = 2. The value −2 is the minimum, not the maximum.

ed41d458-614b-4e23-8c9c-931b0cf5c2a6.subject: accountancy
ed41d458-614b-4e23-8c9c-931b0cf5c2a6.stem: What is the minimum percentage of the issued amount that must be subscribed by the public for a company to proceed with the allotment of shares, as per SEBI guidelines?
ed41d458-614b-4e23-8c9c-931b0cf5c2a6.explanation: As per SEBI guidelines, a company must receive a minimum subscription of 90% of the issue size for public issues.

ede9da50-f9f9-42dc-94d5-6ca964338f4a.subject: physics
ede9da50-f9f9-42dc-94d5-6ca964338f4a.stem: The energy band gap of silicon is 1.1 eV. Taking h = 6.6 × 10^-34 J s, c = 3.0 × 10^8 m s^-1 and 1 eV = 1.6 × 10^-19 J, the longest wavelength of light that can create an electron-hole pair in pure silicon is about
ede9da50-f9f9-42dc-94d5-6ca964338f4a.explanation: A photon creates an electron-hole pair when its energy lifts an electron from the valence band across the band gap into the conduction band, so it needs hc/λ ≥ Eg. The longest wavelength that can do this is λmax = hc/Eg. In joules, Eg = 1.1 × 1.6 × 10^-19 = 1.76 × 10^-19 J, so λmax = (6.6 × 10^-34 × 3.0 × 10^8)/(1.76 × 10^-19) = (1.98 × 10^-25)/(1.76 × 10^-19) ≈ 1.1 × 10^-6 m (about 1100 nm, in the near infrared). Light of longer wavelength has too little energy per photon. Converting 1.1 eV to joules without the factor 1.6 (as 1.1 × 10^-19 J) gives 1.8 × 10^-6 m; dropping c and using h/Eg gives 3.8 × 10^-15 m; asking each photon to supply Eg twice (once for the electron and once for the hole) halves the answer to 5.6 × 10^-7 m, but one photon of energy Eg makes the whole pair.

ee3406d3-0055-4602-935c-270823e4c3d0.subject: physics
ee3406d3-0055-4602-935c-270823e4c3d0.stem: Three small charged beads can slide freely along a smooth, straight insulating thread. The two outer beads each carry +16 nC and are 30 cm apart, and the third bead, of charge q, sits exactly midway between them. For all three beads to stay at rest, q must be:
ee3406d3-0055-4602-935c-270823e4c3d0.explanation: The middle bead is acted on by two equal charges at equal distances (15 cm each) on opposite sides, so the two forces on it cancel whatever q is. Each outer bead must also feel zero net force. An outer bead is repelled by the other outer bead, 30 cm away, with a force k(16 nC)²/(0.30 m)²; this must be cancelled by an equal attraction towards q, which is 15 cm away: k(16 nC)|q|/(0.15 m)². Equating the two, |q| = 16 nC × (0.15/0.30)² = 16 nC/4 = 4 nC. The force from q must pull the positive outer bead inwards, so q is negative: q = −4 nC (in general −Q/4 for equal end charges Q). A charge of +4 nC has the right size but would push both outer beads outwards; −8 nC comes from forgetting to square the distances (−Q/2), and −16 nC from taking both distances as equal (−Q).

f0cb4875-4e15-45cd-9b05-6e2d49d80535.subject: mathematics
options: a point of inflexion at x = 2
f0cb4875-4e15-45cd-9b05-6e2d49d80535.explanation: f′(x) = 3x² − 12x + 12 = 3(x − 2)², so f′(x) = 0 only at x = 2, the one stationary point. For x a little less than 2 and a little more than 2, 3(x − 2)² is positive, so f′ does not change sign as x passes through 2 and f keeps increasing. By the first derivative test, x = 2 is neither a point of local maximum nor a point of local minimum: it is a point of inflexion (f(2) = 13). The second derivative test cannot decide here, because f″(x) = 6x − 12 is 0 at x = 2. Reading f′(x) ≥ 0 as there being no stationary point misses that f′(2) = 0.

f290d5be-ab46-414b-a19b-2068243c7a67.subject: business_studies
f290d5be-ab46-414b-a19b-2068243c7a67.stem: A company that believes consumers will favor products that offer the most quality, performance, and innovative features is following which marketing philosophy?
f290d5be-ab46-414b-a19b-2068243c7a67.explanation: The Product Concept focuses on superior product quality and features.

f9f235e3-5761-49ac-b1f7-8b7d31f956c3.subject: political_science
f9f235e3-5761-49ac-b1f7-8b7d31f956c3.stem: The United Front government formed in 1996 had two Prime Ministers. After the Congress withdrew its outside support and H. D. Deve Gowda lost a confidence vote in April 1997, who became the second United Front Prime Minister?
f9f235e3-5761-49ac-b1f7-8b7d31f956c3.explanation: After the 1996 election the BJP was the largest party, but Atal Bihari Vajpayee's government lasted only 13 days because it could not win a majority. The United Front, a coalition of the Janata Dal and several regional parties, backed by the Left and supported from outside by the Congress, then formed the government with H. D. Deve Gowda as Prime Minister (June 1996 to April 1997). When Congress president Sitaram Kesri withdrew that support, Deve Gowda lost a confidence vote, and the United Front chose I. K. Gujral of the Janata Dal, who had been External Affairs Minister. Gujral was Prime Minister from April 1997 to March 1998: the Congress withdrew support from his government too in November 1997, and he stayed on as caretaker Prime Minister until a new government took office after the 1998 election, when Vajpayee became Prime Minister of a BJP-led coalition in March 1998. V. P. Singh (National Front, 1989-90), Chandra Shekhar (1990-91) and P. V. Narasimha Rao (1991-96) were all Prime Ministers before the United Front.

fb49ae9d-67bf-43c2-a22c-892e32b2e08d.subject: mathematics
fb49ae9d-67bf-43c2-a22c-892e32b2e08d.stem: The maximum value of Z = 3x + 4y, subject to x + y ≤ 4, x + 3y ≤ 6, x ≥ 0 and y ≥ 0, is
fb49ae9d-67bf-43c2-a22c-892e32b2e08d.explanation: The corner points of the feasible region are (0, 0), (4, 0), (3, 1) and (0, 2), where (3, 1) is the intersection of x + y = 4 and x + 3y = 6. Z takes the values 0, 12, 13 and 8 at these points, so the maximum is 13 at (3, 1). The value 16 comes from (0, 4), which violates x + 3y ≤ 6.

fc6098bd-ef63-4d76-8a35-0568d11957ae.subject: physics
fc6098bd-ef63-4d76-8a35-0568d11957ae.stem:
Arrange the following electromagnetic waves in order of increasing wavelength, shortest wavelength first.
(A) Radio waves
(B) Visible light
(C) Gamma rays
(D) Microwaves
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
fc6098bd-ef63-4d76-8a35-0568d11957ae.explanation: Wavelength decreases as frequency increases across the spectrum. Radio waves are the longest, then microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays are the shortest. So increasing wavelength runs gamma rays, visible light, microwaves, radio waves.

fd8df5f2-406a-4a8e-99aa-be5af592e4d2.subject: mathematics
fd8df5f2-406a-4a8e-99aa-be5af592e4d2.stem:
Match List I with List II for the graph of each inequality in the xy-plane.
List I
(A) 3x − 4y ≥ −12
(B) 3x − 4y ≤ −12
(C) 3x − 4y > −12
(D) 3x − 4y < −12
List II
(I) The half-plane that does not contain the origin, without the points of the line 3x − 4y = −12
(II) The half-plane that contains the origin, together with the points of the line 3x − 4y = −12
(III) The half-plane that contains the origin, without the points of the line 3x − 4y = −12
(IV) The half-plane that does not contain the origin, together with the points of the line 3x − 4y = −12
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
fd8df5f2-406a-4a8e-99aa-be5af592e4d2.explanation: The line 3x − 4y = −12, through (−4, 0) and (0, 3), divides the plane into two half-planes. The side an inequality describes is found by testing a point that is not on the line, usually the origin: at (0, 0), 3x − 4y = 0, and 0 > −12. So the origin satisfies 3x − 4y ≥ −12 and 3x − 4y > −12, and does not satisfy 3x − 4y ≤ −12 or 3x − 4y < −12. Whether the line itself belongs to the solution depends on the sign: with ≥ or ≤ the points of the line satisfy the inequality and are included (the line is drawn solid); with > or < they do not, and are excluded: the solution is an open half-plane (the line is drawn dotted). So ≥ gives the origin's side with the line (II), ≤ the other side with the line (IV), > the origin's side without the line (III) and < the other side without the line (I). Taking the ≤ side as the one that holds the origin, without testing, is the common slip: that is true only when the constant on the right is positive, as in x + y ≤ 4. Swapping the boundary rule (strict signs keeping the line) is the other slip.

fdf5673c-1968-42e4-abde-754500ee367e.subject: mathematics
fdf5673c-1968-42e4-abde-754500ee367e.stem: P and Q are square matrices of the same order such that PQ = Q and QP = P. Then which one of the following is true?
fdf5673c-1968-42e4-abde-754500ee367e.explanation: Only the two given products and the associative law of matrix multiplication, (XY)Z = X(YZ), are needed. P² = P · P = P(QP), writing the second P as QP. By the associative law this is (PQ)P = QP = P. In the same way Q² = Q · Q = Q(PQ) = (QP)Q = PQ = Q. So P² = P and Q² = Q: both matrices are idempotent. PQ = Q does not let us cancel Q to get P = I, because Q need not be invertible: for example, P with rows (1, 1) and (0, 0) and Q with rows (1, 0) and (0, 0) satisfy PQ = Q and QP = P, yet neither of them is I; cancelling anyway gives P² = I and Q² = I. Mixing up the two given products in the last step (reading QP as Q, and PQ as P) gives P² = Q and Q² = P, but the same example has P² = P, which is not Q. Working P² out correctly and then cancelling P from QP = P to get Q = I gives P² = P with Q² = I.

ff48d8f7-d70a-4b78-a675-93cd2ad6bc5d.subject: accountancy
ff48d8f7-d70a-4b78-a675-93cd2ad6bc5d.stem: A and B share profits in the ratio 3:2. They admit C for a 1/4 share in the profits, and A and B agree to share the remaining profit equally between themselves. The sacrificing ratio of A and B is:
ff48d8f7-d70a-4b78-a675-93cd2ad6bc5d.explanation: C takes 1/4, so 3/4 is left for A and B. Shared equally, each gets 3/4 × 1/2 = 3/8. Sacrifice = old share − new share. A: 3/5 − 3/8 = 24/40 − 15/40 = 9/40. B: 2/5 − 3/8 = 16/40 − 15/40 = 1/40. Sacrificing ratio = 9/40 : 1/40 = 9:1. The old ratio 3:2 would be the sacrificing ratio only if A and B kept sharing in the old ratio, and 1:1 is the new ratio between them, not what each gave up.
